title: Asian stocks to rise as oil slides after US vote
content_md:
(Nov 5): Asian chipmaking shares fell on Thursday as investors rotated away from the sector after the Democratic sweep in the US midterm election fuelled concern about greater regulation. Treasuries gained.

South Korea’s tech-heavy Kospi Index slid as much as 5.2% with losses driven by the nation’s two giant chipmakers, Samsung Electronics Co and SK Hynix Inc. Futures on the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index also declined. Stocks gained in Hong Kong and Australia as more traditional industries were boosted by lower oil prices.

Treasuries rose for a second day on optimism that lower oil prices will curb inflation, while *Bloomberg*’s gauge of the dollar dropped. Brent crude fell 0.5% to US$94.12 a barrel after tumbling more than 8% on Wednesday following a pledge from Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer to end the Middle East war.

The divergence in global equities results from the sweeping victory of Democrats in the US midterm elections, which has created concern over greater regulatory oversight of high-growth areas such as chipmakers. At the same time, speculation that the party will work to end the Iran war helped to bring down oil prices, benefitting more traditional industries.

“We’re seeing a clear continuation of the rotation out of chipmakers,” said Tim Waterer, the chief market analyst of KCM Trade. “The Democratic sweep raises the real possibility that the AI (artificial intelligence) data-centre buildout hits a regulatory brick wall if the party follows through on its pre-election pledges. That has kept semiconductor names under pressure across the region.”

US stocks are set for gains into year end as the election removes a source of uncertainty, earnings remain strong and lacklustre investor positioning leaves room for renewed buying, according to Scott Rubner, the head of equity and equity derivatives strategy at Citadel Securities.

Since 1946, stocks have been higher one year after every midterm vote, including all four instances when both the House and Senate flipped to the party opposing the president, said Keith Lerner at Truist Advisory Services Inc.

“That supports our base case of giving the bull market the benefit of the doubt, but earnings, the economy, interest rates, valuations, and market trends remain more important to our view,” he added.

While Democrats could complicate data-centre development in some states, many investors see little immediate threat to the AI investment theme that’s powered a rally in stocks tied to the sector.

Greater congressional oversight will not necessarily derail the AI investment cycle as underlying demand is still solid, according to Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi at UBS Global Wealth Management.

“Yes, potential worries over AI regulation are high, but the reality is markets hate uncertainty and now with the election out of the way, we are seeing buyers step in across the board,” said Ryan Detrick at Carson Group.

topic: Chứng khoán châu Á tăng, giá dầu giảm sau bầu cử Mỹ
summary: Cổ phiếu chip châu Á giảm do nhà đầu tư rút khỏi nhóm này sau chiến thắng của đảng Dân chủ trong bầu cử giữa kỳ Mỹ, vì lo ngại quản lý chặt hơn.
Chỉ số Kospi của Hàn Quốc có lúc giảm tới 5,2%, kéo bởi Samsung Electronics và SK Hynix; chứng khoán Hồng Kông và Úc tăng nhờ giá dầu thấp.
Dầu Brent giảm 0,5% xuống 94,12 USD/thùng sau khi giảm hơn 8% hôm thứ Tư, theo bài viết sau cam kết của lãnh đạo phe thiểu số Thượng viện Chuck Schumer về chấm dứt chiến tranh ở Trung Đông.

title: Gần 96% sầu riêng Việt Nam xuất sang Trung Quốc
description: Chín tháng, Trung Quốc chiếm gần 96% kim ngạch xuất khẩu sầu riêng Việt Nam, khiến ngành hàng này gần như không có thị trường thay thế.
content_md:
Chín tháng, Trung Quốc chiếm gần 96% kim ngạch xuất khẩu sầu riêng Việt Nam, khiến ngành hàng này gần như không có thị trường thay thế.

Theo thống kê sơ bộ của Cục Hải quan, 9 tháng đầu năm, Việt Nam thu hơn 3,45 tỷ USD từ xuất khẩu sầu riêng, tăng 25% so với cùng kỳ năm ngoái. Riêng Trung Quốc đại lục đạt gần 3,3 tỷ USD, tăng 27,6%, chiếm gần 96% tổng kim ngạch. Tỷ trọng này cao hơn mức 93,6% của cùng kỳ năm ngoái.

Các thị trường còn lại cách biệt lớn, với Papua New Guinea đứng thứ hai đạt 37,68 triệu USD, Hong Kong 36,7 triệu USD và Mỹ gần 20,5 triệu USD.

Theo ông Đặng Phúc Nguyên, Tổng thư ký Hiệp hội Rau quả Việt Nam, Trung Quốc đại lục là thị trường tiêu thụ đặc biệt quan trọng do người dân nước này chuộng sầu riêng tươi. Trong khi đó, nhiều thị trường khác chủ yếu tiêu thụ sản phẩm cấp đông, tách múi và chế biến.

Sự tập trung này khiến xuất khẩu sầu riêng dễ bị tổn thương nếu Trung Quốc siết kiểm soát chất lượng hoặc giảm nhập khẩu. Ông Nguyên phân tích, sầu riêng có giá trị cao nhưng nhanh chín, khó bảo quản dài ngày nếu không cấp đông sâu. Khi hàng không thể thông quan đúng tiến độ, nguy cơ ùn ứ tại các kho đóng gói ở miền Tây và Tây Nguyên sẽ tăng, kéo theo áp lực bán tháo.

Các thị trường như Mỹ, EU, Nhật Bản, Hàn Quốc hay Australia có tiềm năng nhưng chưa đủ sức hấp thụ lượng sầu riêng tươi nếu bị chuyển hướng trong thời gian ngắn. Theo ông Nguyên, những thị trường này phần lớn tiêu thụ sản phẩm đông lạnh hoặc phục vụ nhóm khách hàng châu Á, nên không thể thay thế Trung Quốc về quy mô đầu ra.

Rủi ro còn thể hiện ở khả năng thương lượng giá của người trồng. Vào chính vụ, khi lượng hàng thu hoạch dồn dập mà đầu ra chủ yếu phụ thuộc vào thông quan sang Trung Quốc, nông dân thường ở thế yếu. Nếu xuất khẩu ách tắc, thương lái có thể giảm mua hoặc ép giá, trong khi người trồng thiếu kho lạnh để giữ hàng chờ thị trường phục hồi.

Thực tế, xuất khẩu sầu riêng năm nay tăng chậm hơn kỳ vọng. Ông Nguyên cho biết giá bán thấp hơn trong chính vụ; vùng trồng miền Tây gặp bất lợi về Cadimi, còn Tây Nguyên có thời tiết mưa nắng thất thường, ảnh hưởng chất lượng và sản lượng. Sầu riêng chế biến tăng tốt hơn đã góp phần kéo kim ngạch chung đi lên.

Để giảm rủi ro phụ thuộc, theo ông Nguyên, trước mắt ngành sầu riêng cần giữ ổn định thị trường Trung Quốc bằng cách kiểm soát chất lượng ngay từ vùng trồng, nhất là dư lượng Cadimi, thuốc bảo vệ thực vật và truy xuất nguồn gốc. Các địa phương cần tăng năng lực xét nghiệm, giám sát mã số vùng trồng và cơ sở đóng gói để hạn chế lô hàng không đạt chuẩn.

Về dài hạn, giới chuyên gia cho rằng doanh nghiệp cần đầu tư kho lạnh, cấp đông và chế biến sâu như tách múi đông lạnh, kem, bánh, bột sầu riêng để kéo dài thời gian bảo quản, thuận lợi vận chuyển đến thị trường xa. Đồng thời, Các doanh nghiệp tập trung khai thác sâu hơn các thị trường có hiệp định thương mại như Hiệp định Đối tác Kinh tế Toàn diện Khu vực (RCEP), Hiệp định Thương mại tự do giữa Việt Nam và Liên minh châu Âu (EU) - EVFTA; tập trung phân khúc cao cấp, hệ thống siêu thị và nhóm khách hàng châu Á tại Mỹ, Nhật Bản, EU, đáp ứng tiêu chuẩn GlobalG.A.P. hoặc hữu cơ.

Ngành cũng cần tăng liên kết giữa Nhà nước, nhà khoa học, doanh nghiệp và nông dân. Doanh nghiệp ký hợp đồng bao tiêu dài hạn với hợp tác xã, phối hợp kế hoạch thu hoạch và đầu tư kho lạnh, logistics tại vùng nguyên liệu để chủ động nguồn cung, giảm áp lực bán gấp khi vào chính vụ hoặc xuất khẩu gián đoạn.

Ông Nguyên dự báo xuất khẩu sầu riêng Việt Nam năm nay có thể đạt 4,5-4,7 tỷ USD, tăng khoảng 20% so với năm ngoái.

content_md:

Nov 4, 2026, 16:44 GMT-5Less than 1 min read

UKOIL−9.26%

Brent crude fell over 8% to settle near $95 a barrel on Wednesday, extending losses for a third consecutive session and hitting a one-month low.

Markets are increasingly pricing in an end to the Iran war after the White House linked Republicans’ midterm election losses to the conflict.

Washington and Tehran have signaled openness to negotiations, with President Donald Trump telling reporters that Iran wants “to make a deal and that could happen.” Trump also cited gasoline prices as a factor behind the Republican defeat, while Vice President JD Vance blamed the war in a post on X. Qatar continues to mediate talks between the two sides.

Trump told the Financial Times that the US had no immediate plans to strike Iran.

Meanwhile, Democratic control of Congress could constrain military spending in the Middle East, further raising hopes for a near-term peace deal.

Supply dynamics also weighed on prices, renewed Gulf exports pushed Middle Eastern oil availability above near-term demand.

"This policy, in our view, is to reduce the pace of CNY’s appreciation against the Dollar, rather than an effort to reverse CNY appreciation trend."

"CNY’s strengthening this year has been supported by China’s large trade surplus and rising corporate FX conversion of proceeds from trade surplus to Reminbi."

"We maintain our USD/CNY forecasts at 6.65 by end-2026 and 6.50 by Q3 2027."

title: Oil prices fall on Vance's post-midterms Iran war repudiation
content_md:
The scale of the GOP losses, which Trump blamed on high oil prices, have turned even his vice president against the idea.

By James Bikales

11/04/2026 3:46 PM EST

Add POLITICO on Google

Share

- Copy link
- X
- Facebook
- Email
- Reddit
- WhatsApp
- LinkedIn

Oil prices extended their sharp selloff on Wednesday as fears that President Donald Trump would launch fresh military strikes on Iran eased a day after Republicans were dealt a sharp defeat in the midterm elections.

Trump has previewed for weeks that he may try to “finish the job” with another round of strikes on Iran. But the scale of the GOP losses has turned even Vice President JD Vance against the idea as voters delivered a sharp repudiation of the war’s impact on prices at the pump.

The U.S. benchmark oil price slipped $6 a barrel on Wednesday after Vance blamed the administration’s war for its losses at the ballot box, bringing the decline to more than $16 since last Thursday. Still, the sharp selloff came too late to help Republicans, who lost their control of the House and Senate Tuesday in an election that focused heavily on cost of living issues.

“The reason we lost is the war,” Vance posted on X Wednesday morning. He also praised Fox News host Rachel Campos-Duffy for advocating a “diplomatic resolution to the conflict.”

A round of promising negotiations in the Middle East earlier this week initiated the pullback in oil prices, with both Iranian and U.S. officials playing up the prospects of a deal. The situation remains highly volatile, however, as the U.S. conducted limited strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz as recently as Monday.

The Treasury Department also announced new sanctions Wednesday on Indian and Turkish entities it said were continuing to support Iran.

“As we have said many times, under Operation Economic Outcast, you are either with us or against us,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. “We know where you are, and we will sanction those who continue supporting the Iranian regime, whether by land, sea, or air.”

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Trump said that high oil prices were probably the “primary reason” for Republicans’ midterm losses, but defended his decision to attack Iran.

“If I had to do it again, I’d have to do it again because long term, it’s the only answer — you can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon,” he said, adding that there is “tremendous oil” flowing out of the Strait of Hormuz.

In an interview with POLITICO late Tuesday, Trump left the door open to further strikes. “We’re going to take a look, and if we see any opportunity to do one thing or another, we’ll do it,” he said.

A renewed military campaign against Iran would come as the supply buffers that have kept a relative lid on oil prices are eroding. The Energy Information Administration reported Wednesday that U.S. diesel inventories fell by another 3.6 million barrels last week and are 13 percent below the five-year average for this time of year.

Claudio Galimberti, chief economist at the consultancy Rystad Energy, said in a research note that the Democratic sweep “changes the political cost of continuing the Iran war.”

“With both chambers now capable of passing resolutions, holding back war funding and delaying confirmations, the administration faces a shorter political runway and greater institutional pressure to find a Hormuz deal,” Galimberti said.

Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis for fuel price tracking website GasBuddy, wrote on X that oil prices were likely to keep dropping as “pressure mounts and Americans loudly deliver a strong statement to politicians.”

“Unless something significant changes, we could be looking at the national average price of gasoline falling below $4/gal in the next week, while diesel could fall below $6 by Thanksgiving,” De Haan added in another post.

To be sure, the Trump administration still has few viable options to get out of the current situation in Iran short of another military campaign, according to Michelle Brouhard, head of policy and geopolitical risk at Kpler.

“A limited strike followed by an exit offers Trump a politically more straightforward off-ramp than accepting Iran’s demands or sustaining an expensive stalemate,” Brouhard said in a research note. “It would allow him to claim victory without making significant concessions.”

Brett Erickson, managing principal of the consulting firm Obsidian Risk Advisors, said the fresh Treasury sanctions on Wednesday were a signal the administration was not stepping back from the conflict.

“The American people delivered a devastating verdict on this war in the midterms, yet not even 24 hours later, the Trump administration is signaling that its economic warfare against Iran will continue nonetheless,” Erickson said in a text message. “Whether through renewed military strikes or escalating economic warfare, both paths risk provoking devastating Iranian retaliation and plunging us back into all-out war.”

December WTI crude oil ( CLZ26) closed down -7.97 (-8.29%) on Wednesday, and December RBOB gasoline ( RBZ26) closed down -0.2069 (-7.05%).

Crude oil and gasoline prices plummeted on Wednesday, with Dec WTI crude oil falling to a 4-week low and gasoline dropping to a 7.75-month low.  Crude prices opened lower on Wednesday when President Trump eased concerns about escalation of the US-Iran war when he played down the prospect of fresh strikes on Iran.  Crude prices were also pressured on Wednesday after weekly EIA crude inventories fell less than expected and US crude production rose to a record.

Losses in crude prices accelerated on Wednesday when Vice President Vance directly attributed the Democratic sweep of Congress in Tuesday’s midterm elections to the Iran war.  Senate Minority Leader Schumer pledged a quick end to the Iran war, saying he had the backing of some Republican lawmakers.  The Democrats' retaking of Congress in the US midterm elections has fueled speculation that the US may try to end the US-Iran conflict sooner rather than later.

Despite the ongoing US-Iran conflict, oil supplies are still leaving the Middle East.  Combined exports from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Iraq, and Kuwait climbed 10% to 15.53 million bpd in October, roughly in line with levels shipped at the start of the year, according to tanker-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg.

Higher Saudi crude output is bearish for crude prices.  Saudi Arabia said its Sep crude production rose by 2 million bpd (+40% m/m) to 8.732 million bpd, recovering from a 36-year low in August.  However, Saudi oil production continues to be threatened by Houthi missile attacks on Saudi Arabia and by the Houthi threats to oil shipments near the Bab-al-Mandeb Strait.

Recent attacks by Ukraine on Russian oil infrastructure have curbed Russian crude production and exports. Ukraine has attacked five of Russia’s ten largest oil-processing plants.  According to EA Analytics, Russian crude-processing rates averaged 3.51 million bpd in July, the lowest in 24 years, amid damage to Russian energy infrastructure caused by drone and missile attacks from Ukraine.  Russian crude processing rates recovered slightly to 3.98 million bpd in September as damaged refineries struggle to come back online.

On the bearish side for crude, the International Energy Agency (IEA) on September 11 warned that high oil prices and restricted oil supply will cause the biggest drop in global oil demand this year since the Covid-19 pandemic.  Despite the projected demand drop, the IEA raised its estimate for this year’s global oil deficit to 1.7 million bpd from last month’s 1.3 million bpd estimate due to the restricted supply caused by the US-Iran war. The IEA said the return of a global oil surplus will be delayed until 2027, later than its previous estimate of late 2026.

On Sunday, OPEC+ agreed to keep oil production quotas unchanged for December.  As a bearish factor for crude, OPEC delegates on August 2 approved their final increase of +188,000 bpd in crude production for September. On paper, the group has restored all 1.65 million bpd of the supply cutback it made in 2023 and said it plans to hold output steady for the rest of the year after the September hike.  However, OPEC+ may struggle to deliver planned production increases amid Middle East shipping disruptions.  OPEC's Sep crude production rose by +1.12 million bpd to 20.71 million bpd.

Vortexa reported Monday that crude oil stored on tankers that have been stationary for at least 7 days fell -11% w/w to 78.36 million bbl in the week ended October 30, the lowest level in more than 3 months.

Wednesday’s weekly EIA report was mixed for crude oil and products.  On the bearish side, EIA crude inventories fell by -865,000 bbl, a smaller draw than expectations of -1.7 million bbl.  Also, crude supplies at Cushing, the delivery point for WTI futures, rose by +280,000 bbl.  In addition, US crude production in the week ended October 30 rose to a record high 14.003 million bpd.  On the bullish side, EIA gasoline supplies unexpectedly fell -222,000 bbl versus expectations of a +1.0 million bbl build.  Also, EIA distillate stockpiles fell -3.57 million bbl to a 23-year low, a larger draw than expectations of -1.5 million bbl.

Wednesday’s EIA report showed that (1) US crude oil inventories as of October 30 were -5.1% below the seasonal 5-year average, (2) gasoline inventories were -0.9% below the seasonal 5-year average, and (3) distillate inventories were -12.7% below the 5-year seasonal average.  In a bearish factor, US crude oil production in the week ending October 30 rose +0.1% w/w to a new record high of 14.003 bpd.

Baker Hughes reported last Friday that the number of active US oil rigs in the week ended October 30 rose by +2 rigs to 462, matching the 1.5-year high of 462 rigs posted on October 9.

#### Beyond Semaglutide? MIRA's Oral Obesity Drug SKNY-1 Shows a Different Weight-Loss Profile in Early Research

Barchart Impact -Mon Nov 2, 7:26AM CSTSponsored Content

This is sponsored content. Barchart is not endorsing the websites or products set forth below.

SKNY-1\_Mira Pharmaceuticals

_**This is sponsored content. Barchart is not endorsing the websites or products set forth below.**_

_In an obesity study in mice, oral SKNY-1 reduced weight and fat without significantly suppressing food intake, while showing favorable lean-mass and weight-regain findings compared with semaglutide._

#### Today's Weight-Loss Drugs Work Well, but Muscle Loss and Weight Regain Remain Open Questions

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 40.3% of U.S. adults had obesity from August 2021 to August 2023. GLP-1 drugs such as semaglutide, the active ingredient in Wegovy® and Ozempic®, have changed how the condition is treated, in part by reducing appetite and food intake.

But two important challenges have followed them: some of the weight lost can come from lean mass, including muscle, and weight often returns after treatment stops.

MIRA Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: MIRA) is pursuing a different approach with SKNY-1, an investigational oral drug candidate for obesity and metabolic disorders. On October 29, it announced initial positive proof-of-concept results from an exploratory pilot study in obese mice, highlighting promising findings related to weight reduction, lean mass, and post-treatment weight regain compared with semaglutide. Read the full press release here.

#### **The Mice Lost Significant Weight and Fat Without Eating Significantly Less**

Oral SKNY-1 produced statistically significant reductions in body weight and fat mass compared with vehicle-treated controls, and most of the treatment-associated weight difference came from fat.

Notably, these reductions occurred without a statistically significant decrease in food consumption.

These findings raise the possibility that SKNY-1 influences energy expenditure or other metabolic pathways involved in weight regulation.

#### SKNY-1 Was Compared With Semaglutide on Food Intake, Lean Mass and Weight Regain

While demonstrating efficacy against vehicle-treated controls is an important first step, comparing SKNY-1 with semaglutide, one of the most widely used obesity treatments, provides additional insight into its potential differentiation.. The study identified three potential areas of differentiation from the semaglutide reference group.

The first was food intake. SKNY-1 produced significant reductions in body weight and fat mass without a statistically significant decrease in food consumption, suggesting a potentially different approach to weight regulation.

The second was lean mass. At the Day 14 body-composition assessment, mice treated with oral SKNY-1 did not show statistically significant lean-mass loss relative to vehicle controls. In contrast, semaglutide-treated mice showed statistically significant lean-mass loss relative to vehicle controls.

The third was post-treatment weight regain.. During a two-week observation period, SKNY-1-treated mice showed slow and limited weight regain, with no statistically significant increase in food consumption. In contrast, Semaglutide-treated mice experienced rapid and substantial weight rebound, along with a statistically significant increase in food consumption relative to vehicle controls.

Loss of lean mass and weight regain after treatment discontinuation are two important concerns associated with GLP-1 therapies.. In a 2022 extension of semaglutide's STEP 1 trial, participants regained about two-thirds of their lost weight within a year of stopping. That makes the comparison noteworthy, even at this early stage.

#### The New Mouse Data Build on Earlier Zebrafish Research That Showed About 30% Weight Reduction

SKNY-1 is a cannabinoid analog being investigated for its effects on biological pathways involved in metabolic regulation.

In earlier peer-reviewed research in a zebrafish model of obesity, SKNY-1 produced approximately 30% weight reduction. That study also showed maintenance of whole-body density, reduced fat buildup in the liver, and changes in appetite-related signaling.

The new pilot study extends that research into a mammalian obesity model. According to Itzchak Angel, Ph.D., MIRA's Chief Scientific Advisor, the results build on earlier findings and support the hypothesis that SKNY-1 may influence energy expenditure or other metabolic pathways involved in weight regulation.

For investors, this progression is meaningful because SKNY-1's evidence now spans more than one species and more than one study, providing additional support for its potential as a differentiated obesity treatment.

#### The Next Study Will Directly Measure Whether SKNY-1 Increases Energy Expenditure

MIRA plans to test the energy-expenditure hypothesis directly. Its next study will measure energy expenditure and other metabolic parameters while further characterizing SKNY-1's effects on body composition and weight regulation.

MIRA is also advancing longer-term preclinical studies of SKNY-1, alongside ongoing IND-enabling activities and chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) development, to support its progression toward clinical trials.

"Obesity represents one of the largest and fastest-growing opportunities in healthcare, with the potential for multiple multibillion-dollar therapies," said Erez Aminov, Chief Executive Officer of MIRA Pharmaceuticals. "We believe the future of obesity treatment will extend beyond a single class of drugs."

#### SKNY-1 Gives MIRA a Third Oral Program Alongside Two Pain Drug Candidates

SKNY-1 joins two pain programs in MIRA's pipeline. Ketamir-2 has completed Phase 1 and is advancing toward Phase 2 clinical development for neuropathic pain, beginning with chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, under an active IND. MIRA-55, a candidate for inflammatory pain, recently demonstrated pain relief comparable to celecoxib (Celebrex) in a three-week preclinical study. Following scientific review, the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration determined that none of the three candidates is a controlled substance.

SKNY-1 remains an investigational preclinical program, and its safety and efficacy in humans have not been established. But for investors following the next generation of obesity treatments, it now presents a potentially differentiated approach: significant weight and fat reduction without a statistically significant decrease in food intake, favorable findings on lean mass and post-treatment weight regain compared with semaglutide in mice, and a planned study designed to further investigate its underlying metabolic mechanism.

For more on SKNY-1's results in obese mice, read MIRA Pharmaceuticals' full press release here.

title: Oil prices drop below $100 as midterms fuel hope for an end to the Iran war
content_md:
Oil prices dropped sharply Wednesday, propelled by growing hopes for a resolution in the Iran war.

European Brent crude fell below $100 per barrel for the first time since Oct. 7. The move translated to a nearly $8 drop, or an 8.3% decline. U.S. crude oil, or West Texas Intermediate, also slipped 8.3% to close at about $88.12. It was oil’s biggest daily decline since April.

Relief for consumers may follow. Oil’s fall could bring the national average price of gas down below $4 in the “days ahead,” Patrick De Haan, an analyst at GasBuddy, said.

Prices moved lower as trading desks and energy experts watched closely for a sign that Tuesday’s midterm election results would pressure President Donald Trump into ending the Iran war without a major escalation. The war sent gasoline and diesel prices skyrocketing, making already stubborn inflation worse for American consumers, farmers and business owners.

“The next six weeks typically deliver one of the most hostile environments for higher gasoline and diesel prices,” Tom Kloza, chief energy adviser to Gulf Oil, said on social media. “If the US or Iran don’t pursue ‘scorched earth’ policies in the Persian Gulf, we may see considerably lower prices by second half December.”

On Wednesday morning, that average price was $4.12. That’s 39% higher than before Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu launched the Iran war Feb. 28, which snarled shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz.

On social media, Vice President JD Vance said the war is the reason the Republican Party suffered such steep losses in the midterm elections.

“And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there,” said Vance, who could be the GOP’s standard-bearer in the 2028 presidential election.

Trump also said he realized the toll the Iran war took on American consumers.

“I think it’s the gasoline price,” Trump said Tuesday night on Fox News as the first results became clear. “People agree with what I’m doing on Iran, but they really probably weren’t willing to do the short-term consequence of paying more for gasoline, and that, you know, I understand that.”

Oil’s drop over the last three trading sessions has been precipitous. On Friday, Brent oil traded as high as $118 per barrel, but by Wednesday, its price was around $94.

Despite the sharp move lower, the overall price of oil remains higher by 60% compared with the start of the year.

On Tuesday, 59% of voters who went to the ballot box told NBC News in an exit poll that they were “very concerned” with the cost of gas and diesel fuel, echoing concerns that consumers have voiced for months.

But diesel fuel prices have economists far more concerned.

U.S. diesel futures also tumbled Wednesday. As of midday, prices declined by nearly 7%, to their lowest level since the end of August. That likely means that more relief is coming for prices at the pump.

As the fuel that powers transportation services for goods, such as groceries, across the country, any jump in prices could quickly ripple across the economy through higher prices on store shelves.

title: Chinese Yuan: PBoC cools appreciation trend – Commerzbank
content_md:
TRENDING:

Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay and Dr. Henry Hao highlight that the People’s Bank of China raised the FX reserve requirement ratio to slow rapid CNY gains after a 13-session winning streak. They stress the move is counter-cyclical, aimed at preserving two-way flexibility rather than reversing the appreciation trend, and note USD/CNY and USD/CNH both bounced to 6.67 on the announcement.

#### PBoC leans against rapid CNY gains

"The People’s Bank of China (PBoC) moved to cool CNY appreciation yesterday, raising the foreign-currency reserve requirement ratio (FX RRR) by 2%-points to 6%, effective 15 November. The announcement prompted a reversal in CNY following 13 consecutive sessions of gains, the longest winning streak since 1996."

"The move was unexpected, reinforcing the PBoC's resistance to rapid currency appreciation. The gap between the PBoC’s daily fixing at 6.7150 and our estimated fixing rate of 6.6516 widened to 634 pips, the largest divergence since 10 September."

"The mechanics of the hike work by forcing banks to lock up a larger share of FX deposits, draining dollar liquidity from the onshore system and easing upward pressure on CNY. The move mirrors a similar playbook deployed in 2021, when the PBoC raised the FX RRR twice to lean against yuan strength."

"However, the measure is likely to slow the pace of appreciation than reverse the underlying trend, which remains supported by the large trade surplus."

"The FX RRR hike is widely read as a counter-cyclical signal rather than a directional reversal. The PBoC appears intent on preserving two-way flexibility and preventing appreciation expectations from becoming self-reinforcing, particularly as global investors have begun joining domestic exporters on the yuan-buying side. Further PBoC action, such as lowering the macro-prudential adjustment parameters, cannot be ruled out if appreciation pressures resume."

title: Onshore yuan snaps winning streak as PBOC lifts FX reserve ratio
content_md:
(Nov 3): The onshore yuan ended its longest winning streak in three decades after the People’s Bank of China moved to cool its rally by asking banks to hold more foreign currencies in reserve.

The yuan weakened as much as 0.4% to 6.6731 per dollar onshore, halting 13 straight days of gains, which was the longest streak since 1996, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. It also dropped as much as 0.4% in offshore trading. The PBOC’s move forces banks to lock up more foreign exchange, reducing the supply of dollars and easing the appreciation pressure on the yuan.

The move is “aimed at moderating the pace of yuan appreciation rather than reversing its direction”, said Cindy Keung, economist at OCBC Bank (Hong Kong). “While the official objective is to strengthen foreign exchange liquidity management, the move also sends a clear policy signal that authorities are seeking to prevent excessive and rapid yuan appreciation.”

The yuan has advanced over 4% against the greenback this year to outperform most of its Asian peers, thanks to surging exports, heavy corporate conversion flows and the central bank’s tolerance for a stronger currency. That resilience has held up even as mounting expectations of Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes bolstered the dollar.

The central bank will increase the ratio by two percentage points from the current 4% to 6%, according to a statement. The move takes effect on Nov 15. The PBOC last raised the ratio in December 2021, when it asked financial institutions to hold 9% of their foreign exchange in reserve. It was the second increase that year, after the central bank raised the ratio by two percentage points in June.

“The move will withdraw about US$24 billion (RM97.78 billion) from the market,” said Zhaopeng Xing, senior China strategist at Australia & New Zealand Banking Group, referring to the latest reduction. “It is relatively low comparing with net FX sales monthly US$30 billion this year. The move is symbolic. More measures will be possible if market imbalance remains in place.”

The PBOC also set its daily reference rate more than 600 pips weaker than estimates on Tuesday, the largest bias since early September. The so-called fixing limits the onshore yuan’s movements to 2% on either side of the reference rate, signalling official pushback against rapid appreciation.

The latest central bank measures also come amid expectations that the currency would benefit from seasonal tailwinds. Exporters typically step up yuan purchases around year-end to meet accounting and pre-Lunar New Year funding needs, contributing to the currency’s seasonal strength. As cross-border e-commerce becomes a larger source of China’s trade surplus, global holiday shopping may be turning into a more meaningful driver of yuan demand.

“It is ahead of the FX sales season in 4Q. The tightening will help rebalance the flows and slow the appreciation pace of the yuan,” said ANZ’s Xing.

For Fiona Lim, a senior FX strategist at Malayan Banking Berhad, the timing of the PBOC’s move is likely linked to global political events.

“Given that it happens just before the US midterm elections, this could be to prevent yuan appreciation from gathering pace in an environment of lower oil \[and a\] Democrat sweep that could be negative for the dollar,” she said.

title: Democrats' Midterm Surge Sinks Dollar, Rattles Asian Stocks as Divided Washington Looms
content_md:
A strong showing by Democrats in the U.S. midterm elections knocked the dollar lower and weighed on Asian equities on Wednesday, as investors began to price in the prospect of a divided Congress that could stall President Donald Trump's legislative agenda for his final two years in office.

The party was on track to win control of both the House and the Senate, according to early results, after capturing North Carolina in a race that had been seen as too close to call. Prediction markets reflected the shift: Polymarket put the odds of a Democratic House at 100% and a Senate win at 99%. The outcome would mark a sharp rebuke of Republican governance and hand Democrats a narrow but consequential majority in a chamber Republicans had controlled 53-47.

Markets have generally favored divided government in Washington, on the view that it lowers the risk of sweeping policy shifts. But analysts cautioned that the size of the Democratic wave matters. "A narrow blue wave may be largely priced in," said Chris Weston of Pepperstone. "A commanding one could force markets to rethink Trump's remaining policy agenda and the political trajectory into 2028." Weston added that Democratic control of Congress would raise the odds of "legislative gridlock, fiscal brinkmanship, debt-ceiling disputes, and congressional investigations," while noting that the president retains considerable executive authority, leaving the sector-by-sector implications far from clear.

Stephen Brown of Capital Economics argued the near-term policy outlook was not dramatically altered, citing the Democrats' lack of a filibuster-proof Senate majority and Trump's veto power. Trump himself told CBS in a telephone interview on Tuesday that he would act as "Mr Veto" and block Democratic legislation should the party prevail.

The dollar weakened against the yen, with the greenback buying 158.06 yen versus 158.75 late Tuesday, while the euro climbed to $1.1249 from $1.1191 and sterling rose to $1.3465 from $1.3413. Treasury yields also slipped, with the 10-year note's yield easing to 4.96% from 4.91%, as observers noted that gridlock in Washington tends to restrain spending. "Typically, when we get a divided government, it has been historically pretty good for Treasuries," said Brij Khurana of Wellington Management.

Asian equities bore the brunt of the risk-off mood. Tokyo's Nikkei 225 tumbled 3.6% to 60,835.36, pressured by a stronger yen that hurts exporters. Chipmaker Kioxia Holdings plunged more than 13%, while Advantest and SoftBank Group each lost more than 8%. In Seoul, SK Hynix fell as much as 3% and Samsung Electronics slipped almost 2%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index shed 0.4% to 23,428.32, Shanghai's Composite edged down 0.1% to 3,606.18, and Sydney's S&P/ASX 200 dropped 1.1% to 10,638.43.

Technology shares remained under pressure as investors continued to question the scale of spending on artificial intelligence and when returns might materialize. In the prior U.S. session, the S&P 500 gained 0.4% even as most of its constituents declined, lifted by Nvidia and Broadcom, while Microsoft, Amazon and Meta Platforms each rose more than 2%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.4%, or 197 points, to 51,786.72, and the Nasdaq composite added 0.8%.

Oil prices extended Tuesday's decline as traders monitored the Middle East after Trump confirmed U.S. strikes on Iran but played down speculation that bombing would resume once the election concluded. "We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it," he told the Financial Times. West Texas Intermediate slipped 0.5% to $96.65 a barrel and Brent crude lost 0.2% to $103.41.

The election result injects a new layer of political uncertainty into markets already consumed by AI valuation concerns and elevated inflation and interest rates. A Congress unable to advance major legislation would limit fiscal stimulus but also raise the risk of standoffs over the debt ceiling, a scenario that could periodically unsettle bond investors. For equity markets, the immediate focus is likely to remain on the AI trade and corporate earnings, with the political backdrop in Washington serving as a secondary, if persistent, source of volatility.

title: Trump Declares Iran Wants a 'Settlement ASAP' Amid 'Dropping' Oil Prices
content_md:
President Donald Trump suggested on November 2 that a deal with Iran could be approaching, *RadarOnline* can report.

Trump, 80, pointed to the falling oil prices as evidence that Iran had been weakened and was increasingly willing to negotiate a settlement on his terms.

#### Trump’s Diplomatic Signals

Trump wrote on Truth Social: “Oil Prices are DROPPING LIKE A ROCK, down almost $10 a Barrel, A RECORD, because people feel that there will not be a War with Iran. Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible. It could happen!”

He told *Axios* in a phone interview that he was “in no rush” to decide on another military offensive, saying: “One way or the other, we will do something, but there is no rush. We crippled them financially. They have no money, no gasoline, and their people are getting very tired of it.”

Trump added that negotiations were “going fine” and that Iran wanted a deal “more than they ever wanted.”

When asked whether he would resume strikes after the midterms, he answered “no,” according to the media pool.

*Bloomberg* reported that Iran’s supreme leader had approved the government’s pursuit of negotiations and that Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu he wanted to allow talks to play out.

#### Oil Prices Continue to Plunge

Oil prices recorded their steepest daily decline in about three months.

Advertisement

U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell 7.4 percent to close at $96.46 per barrel, their largest single-day drop since July 27.

Brent crude dropped 7.6 percent to settle at $104.77 per barrel.

The selloff pushed the U.S. benchmark below the $100 threshold. European natural gas futures fell nearly 11 percent at one point, and U.S. heating oil recorded its steepest decline in six months.

#### Trump Declared War in Iran Was 'Won' Before Midterms

Trump’s comments marked a shift from the previous week, when CNN reported he was “leaning toward” ordering major strikes after the midterms, with U.S. forces allegedly prepared to launch an operation within four days of authorization.

However, in recent remarks at the Lincoln Memorial, Trump declared, “We had a war with Iran. We won.”

“I don’t even know if you call it a war because we haven’t been doing any fighting for months, you know?” he said at the time. “We control the Strait of Hormuz. We control it and strongly control it.”

#### Unresolved Risks

Despite diplomatic signals, Washington and Tehran have not reached an agreement on fully reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Shipping companies face security concerns, and previous negotiations have failed to produce lasting peace.

title: ECB: Interest Rate Hike In December Almost Certain
content_md:
Μake us preferred on Google

The rise in inflation to its highest level in three years makes a new ECB interest rate hike in December more likely.

According to data published by Eurostat on Wednesday, inflation in the 21 countries that use the euro rose to 4% in October from 3.8% the previous month, in line with economists’ forecasts in a Reuters poll, with energy inflation reaching 20%.

At the same time, core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, remained unchanged at 2.5%, in line with forecasts. This suggests that second-round effects, which have been a concern for some time, have not yet materialized.

“Despite the lack of evidence of second-round effects, today’s inflation data further strengthens the case for an ECB rate hike in December. The central bank is concerned that the longer the energy shock lasts, the greater the risk that broader inflationary pressures become entrenched,” Nicola Nobile of Oxford Economics told Reuters.

This year, inflation has quickly risen above the ECB’s 2% target, as the US conflict with Iran drove up energy costs. This is being passed on to retail prices, affecting an economic area that imports the vast majority of the energy it consumes.

#### **Monetary Policy**

The ECB kept interest rates unchanged last week. However, members of the central bank’s Governing Council, including the influential heads of the central banks of Germany and Italy, have already signaled that a new move in December is now considered likely.

Financial markets are pricing in two to three hikes to the ECB’s deposit rate (currently at 2.5%) over the next year, with expectations shifting frequently in line with oil prices.

Meanwhile, Sweden’s central bank followed the example of other central banks on Wednesday, tightening monetary policy and signaling further hikes amid fears that energy inflation could spread to the wider economy.

The Bank of England, which meets on Thursday, is expected to move in the same direction, raising its key interest rate to 4.00%, as it also forecasts that inflation will exceed 4% early next year.

#### **Concern Over Food Prices**

In a development that may worry the ECB, food inflation continued to accelerate, with unprocessed food prices rising 4.6% compared with the previous year.

This item makes up only a small part of the consumer price basket, but it includes some of the products households buy most often. According to economists, rapid price changes could have a disproportionately large effect on inflation expectations.

Services inflation, the largest component of the consumer price basket, rose to 3.3% from 3.2%, while industrial goods prices increased by 1.2%, compared with 1.1% the previous month.

Although Wednesday’s data shows that energy inflation is not yet causing second-round effects, the high cost of diesel and natural gas risks being passed on to the prices of other goods and services, causing indirect effects that are expected to last.

At the same time, low natural gas storage levels create a significant risk of further increases in heating costs, economists note.

This may not yet be visible in the current data, but it will likely show up in the coming months, especially in January, when the prices of certain goods are traditionally adjusted.

The ECB now expects inflation to remain above 4% for most of the first half of 2027, before falling quickly to levels just above 2%, as the high figures from the same period of the previous year drop out of the data.

title: Oil prices drop below $100 for the first time in nearly a month
content_md:
Oil prices dropped sharply Wednesday, propelled by growing hopes for a resolution in the Iran war.

European Brent crude fell below $100 per barrel for the first time since Oct. 7. The move translated to a nearly $8 drop, or an 8.3% decline. U.S. crude oil, or West Texas Intermediate, also slipped 8.3% to close at about $88.12. It was oil's biggest daily decline since April.

Relief for consumers may follow. Oil's fall could bring the national average price of gas down below $4 in the "days ahead," Patrick De Haan, an analyst at GasBuddy, said.

Prices moved lower as trading desks and energy experts watched closely for a sign that Tuesday's midterm election results would pressure President Donald Trump into ending the Iran war without a major escalation. The war sent gasoline and diesel prices skyrocketing, making already stubborn inflation worse for American consumers, farmers and business owners.

"The next six weeks typically deliver one of the most hostile environments for higher gasoline and diesel prices," Tom Kloza, chief energy adviser to Gulf Oil, said on social media. "If the US or Iran don't pursue 'scorched earth' policies in the Persian Gulf, we may see considerably lower prices by second half December."

On Wednesday morning, that average price was $4.12. That's 39% higher than before Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu launched the Iran war Feb. 28, which snarled shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz.

On social media, Vice President JD Vance said the war is the reason the Republican Party suffered such steep losses in the midterm elections.

"And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there," said Vance, who could be the GOP's standard-bearer in the 2028 presidential election.

Trump also said he realized the toll the Iran war took on American consumers.

"I think it's the gasoline price," Trump said Tuesday night on Fox News as the first results became clear. "People agree with what I'm doing on Iran, but they really probably weren't willing to do the short-term consequence of paying more for gasoline, and that, you know, I understand that."

Oil's drop over the last three trading sessions has been precipitous. On Friday, Brent oil traded as high as $118 per barrel, but by Wednesday, its price was around $94.

Despite the sharp move lower, the overall price of oil remains higher by 60% compared with the start of the year.

On Tuesday, 59% of voters who went to the ballot box told NBC News in an exit poll that they were "very concerned" with the cost of gas and diesel fuel, echoing concerns that consumers have voiced for months.

title: Khu gần 3.800 căn hộ Thủ Thiêm dự kiến có tổng vốn đầu tư hơn 39.800 tỷ đồng
description: Ngoài 18.253 tỷ đồng giá khởi điểm đất và tài sản hiện hữu, nhà đầu tư trúng đấu giá 3.790 căn hộ tại Thủ Thiêm dự kiến cần thêm gần 21.590 tỷ đồng cho đầu tư xây dựng.
content_md:
Ngoài 18.253 tỷ đồng giá khởi điểm đất và tài sản hiện hữu, nhà đầu tư trúng đấu giá 3.790 căn hộ tại Thủ Thiêm dự kiến cần thêm gần 21.590 tỷ đồng cho đầu tư xây dựng.

Theo phương án đấu giá quyền sử dụng đất và tài sản gắn liền với đất tại 5 khu đất với 3.790 căn hộ thuộc khu tái định cư Bình Khánh cũ, phường An Khánh, được UBND TP HCM phê duyệt ngày 3/11, tổng mức đầu tư dự kiến cho quỹ tài sản này gần 39.844 tỷ đồng.

Trong đó, hơn 18.253 tỷ đồng là giá khởi điểm đấu giá quyền sử dụng đất và tài sản gắn liền với đất. Khoảng 21.590 tỷ đồng còn lại là tổng mức đầu tư xây dựng dự kiến mà chủ đầu tư trúng đấu giá sẽ phải bỏ ra để đầu tư khai thác, cải tạo và phát triển quỹ tài sản này. Khoản vốn xây dựng chưa bao gồm thuế giá trị gia tăng.

Theo giải thích của TP HCM, tổng vốn đầu tư dự kiến này là cơ sở xác định điều kiện về vốn chủ sở hữu của người tham gia đấu giá theo quy định. Tổng vốn đầu tư thực tế được xác định trên cơ sở giá trúng đấu giá, hồ sơ dự án đầu tư và các chi phí hợp pháp có liên quan.

Như vậy, doanh nghiệp tham gia đấu giá dự án này phải có vốn chủ sở hữu tối thiểu bằng 20% tổng vốn đầu tư dự kiến. Nếu tính trên tổng vốn của cả 5 khu đất, mức vốn tương ứng gần 7.969 tỷ đồng.

Năm khu đất trước đây được ký hiệu R1 đến R5, nay mang tên quy hoạch mới từ 1.K7.5.HH đến 1.K7.9.HH. Trong tổng mức đầu tư xây dựng dự kiến, lô R1 rộng 3,14 ha, chiếm khoản lớn nhất với khoảng 8.618 tỷ đồng; R4 (rộng 1,96ha) với 5.372 tỷ đồng. Các khu còn lại gồm R5, R2 và R3 lần lượt có mức đầu tư hơn 3.351 tỷ đồng, 2.237 tỷ đồng và hơn 2.011 tỷ đồng.

Theo quy hoạch điều chỉnh được phường An Khánh phê duyệt ngày 30/9, cả 5 khu đất được chuyển sang chức năng hỗn hợp nhà ở và dịch vụ. Trong đó, R1 có tỷ lệ diện tích chức năng dịch vụ cao nhất, chiếm 38%, phần nhà ở chiếm 61,8%. Với bốn khu còn lại, chức năng nhà ở chiếm khoảng 86-87%, dịch vụ khoảng 12-14%.

Quỹ 3.790 căn hộ tại Khu đô thị mới Thủ Thiêm thuộc khu tái định cư Bình Khánh cũ, được xây dựng bằng vốn ngân sách trong chương trình 12.500 căn hộ phục vụ người dân bị giải tỏa để thực hiện Khu đô thị mới Thủ Thiêm. Các khối nhà hoàn thành năm 2015 nhưng không được đưa vào sử dụng trong thời gian dài, khiến nhiều hạng mục xuống cấp.

TP HCM từng bốn lần tổ chức đấu giá quỹ căn hộ này nhưng đều không thành công. Giá khởi điểm tăng từ 8.800 tỷ đồng năm 2017 lên khoảng 9.900 tỷ đồng trong các lần đấu giá năm 2021 và 2023.

Bên cạnh quy mô tài sản lớn, hiện trạng xuống cấp và bài toán khai thác sau khi nhận chuyển nhượng cũng có thể khiến nhà đầu tư phải tính đến khoản vốn đáng kể để cải tạo công trình, nâng cấp hệ thống kỹ thuật, hạ tầng và tiện ích. Đây là những yếu tố làm tăng chi phí đầu tư, đồng thời gây khó khăn cho việc tìm kiếm nhà đầu tư phù hợp.

Đến năm 2025, thành phố thống nhất chủ trương chuyển đổi công năng quỹ căn hộ từ nhà tái định cư sang nhà ở thương mại nhằm tăng khả năng khai thác.

title: Dollar Slides and Gold Surges After Democrats Sweep Both Chambers in 2026 Midterms
content_md:
The dollar didn't just fall on Wednesday — it got a reality check. The US Dollar Index (DXY) tumbled to its lowest level in five weeks, grazing 101.26 as investors processed a sweeping Democratic victory in the 2026 midterm elections. The speed of the selloff spoke for itself: despite scattered analyst warnings, markets had not fully priced in this outcome heading into Election Day.

CBS News projected Democratic control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, with the party flipping at least seven Senate seats and 27 congressional districts across the country. Exit polls placed President Trump's approval rating at 38% — historically low for a sitting president at the midterm mark.

#### Gridlock as a Market Force

For currency traders, a divided government carries a straightforward message: less fiscal stimulus, lower inflation pressure from Washington and reduced upward momentum for the dollar. With Democrats poised to control both chambers, Trump's signature economic priorities — extended tax cuts, expanded tariffs and accelerated deregulation — now face significant legislative obstacles.

The resulting uncertainty pushed Treasury yields lower, stripping away one of the greenback's last structural supports heading into year-end. The DXY closed Wednesday at 101.4290, down 0.43% from the prior session and roughly 0.72% lower over the past month. The index's 52-week range runs between 95.55 and 102.94.

#### Gold Reclaims $4,000

No asset celebrated the electoral results more visibly than gold. The yellow metal surged back above $4,000 per ounce on Wednesday, posting nearly 3% in intraday gains after briefly dipping below $3,900 in late October.

The dynamics were self-reinforcing: a weaker dollar makes gold cheaper for buyers operating in other currencies, while political uncertainty boosts its appeal as a store of value. XAU/USD traded near $4,041 during the session, extending gains fueled by record gold ETF holdings — 4,256 tonnes globally — and steady central bank accumulation of 321 net tonnes in the third quarter alone.

#### Tech Stocks, Iran and the Wider Fallout

Beyond the legislative freeze, markets began pricing in sector-specific consequences. Democratic control of Congress could usher in stricter regulatory frameworks for artificial intelligence and tighter corporate oversight, dampening near-term growth expectations for the technology sector. Tech stocks showed mixed performance through Wednesday's session.

Separately, investors kept a close watch on the possibility of renewed US military action against Iran following the elections, as diplomatic negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain at an impasse. The geopolitical overhang in the Middle East continues to complicate any sustained recovery for the greenback.

#### Technical Picture and What Comes Next

The DXY carries a bearish short-term bias after breaking below its 200-period simple moving average on the four-hour chart. The immediate technical floor sits near 101.25; a sustained close beneath that level would open a path toward September lows.

Looking ahead, traders are turning their attention to upcoming labor market data and central bank rate decisions in the United Kingdom, Australia, Norway and Sweden — the next potential catalysts that will determine whether the dollar stages a recovery or deepens its decline.

Wednesday's session made one thing clear: in 2026, the US dollar doesn't move on Fed policy alone. Washington's political weather has become a market force in its own right.

December WTI crude oil ( CLZ26) is down -3.99 (-4.15%) today, and December RBOB gasoline ( RBZ26) is down -0.1023 (-3.48%).

Crude oil and gasoline prices are sharply lower today, with Dec WTI crude oil falling to a 3-week low and gasoline dropping to a 3-month low.  Comments today from President Trump eased concerns about escalation of the US-Iran war when he played down the prospect of fresh strikes on Iran.  Crude prices fell further today after weekly EIA crude inventories fell less than expected and oil supplies at Cushing rose.

Crude oil prices fell today on comments from President Trump, who said he had no immediate plans to launch strikes on Iran following the midterm elections.  Also, Democrats' retaking of Congress in the US midterm elections has fueled speculation that the US may try to end the US-Iran conflict sooner rather than later.

Despite the ongoing US-Iran conflict, oil supplies are still leaving the Middle East.  Combined exports from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Iraq, and Kuwait climbed 10% to 15.53 million bpd in October, roughly in line with levels shipped at the start of the year, according to tanker-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg.

Higher Saudi crude output is bearish for crude prices.  Saudi Arabia said its Sep crude production rose by 2 million bpd (+40% m/m) to 8.732 million bpd, recovering from a 36-year low in August.  However, Saudi oil production continues to be threatened by Houthi missile attacks on Saudi Arabia and by the Houthi threats to oil shipments near the Bab-al-Mandeb Strait.

Recent attacks by Ukraine on Russian oil infrastructure have curbed Russian crude production and exports. Ukraine has attacked five of Russia’s ten largest oil-processing plants.  According to EA Analytics, Russian crude-processing rates averaged 3.51 million bpd in July, the lowest in 24 years, amid damage to Russian energy infrastructure caused by drone and missile attacks from Ukraine.  Russian crude processing rates recovered slightly to 3.98 million bpd in September as damaged refineries struggle to come back online.

On the bearish side for crude, the International Energy Agency (IEA) on September 11 warned that high oil prices and restricted oil supply will cause the biggest drop in global oil demand this year since the Covid-19 pandemic.  Despite the projected demand drop, the IEA raised its estimate for this year’s global oil deficit to 1.7 million bpd from last month’s 1.3 million bpd estimate due to the restricted supply caused by the US-Iran war. The IEA said the return of a global oil surplus will be delayed until 2027, later than its previous estimate of late 2026.

On Sunday, OPEC+ agreed to keep oil production quotas unchanged for December.  As a bearish factor for crude, OPEC delegates on August 2 approved their final increase of +188,000 bpd in crude production for September. On paper, the group has restored all 1.65 million bpd of the supply cutback it made in 2023 and said it plans to hold output steady for the rest of the year after the September hike.  However, OPEC+ may struggle to deliver planned production increases amid Middle East shipping disruptions.  OPEC's Sep crude production rose by +1.12 million bpd to 20.71 million bpd.

Vortexa reported Monday that crude oil stored on tankers that have been stationary for at least 7 days fell -11% w/w to 78.36 million bbl in the week ended October 30, the lowest level in more than 3 months.

Today’s weekly EIA report was mixed for crude oil and products.  On the bearish side, EIA crude inventories fell by -865,000 bbl, a smaller draw than expectations of -1.7 million bbl.  Also, crude supplies at Cushing, the delivery point for WTI futures, rose by +280,000 bbl. In addition, US crude production in the week ended October 30 rose to a record high 14.003 million bpd.  On the bullish side, EIA gasoline supplies unexpectedly fell -222,000 bbl versus expectations of a +1.0 million bbl build.  Also, EIA distillate stockpiles fell -3.57 million bbl to a 23-year low, a larger draw than expectations of -1.5 million bbl.

Today’s EIA report showed that (1) US crude oil inventories as of October 30 were -5.1% below the seasonal 5-year average, (2) gasoline inventories were -0.9% below the seasonal 5-year average, and (3) distillate inventories were -12.7% below the 5-year seasonal average.  In a bearish factor, US crude oil production in the week ending October 30 rose +0.1% w/w to a new record high of 14.003 bpd.

Baker Hughes reported last Friday that the number of active US oil rigs in the week ended October 30 rose by +2 rigs to 462, matching the 1.5-year high of 462 rigs posted on October 9.

title: Will the Federal Reserve’s Rate Hike Derail Bank Funding Cost Gains?
content_md:
Nov 04, 2026, 11:00 AM GMT-5 | By Frank Gargano
The Federal Reserve’s decision to raise interest rates for the first time in more than three years, coupled with last month’s rate hold, could undo a beneficial trend for U.S. banks that have enjoyed steadily declining funding and deposit costs over the past two years.

The central bank voted to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points (bps) in September to 3.75%-4.0%, as persistently elevated inflation remained too big of a problem for members of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) to leave unaddressed. “Our predominant focus is on the price stability side of our mandate, as inflation has been too high for too long,” said Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh during the September FOMC press conference on September 16.

Now, in the wake of the October decision to hold rates steady and murmurs of a second rate hike before the end of the year, banking leaders are wondering whether funding costs could start climbing once again.

To better understand the historical context behind these trends and how the banking industry is positioned to handle the current interest rate environment, KBRA Financial Intelligence (KFI) examined trends in deposit costs, funding expenses, and net interest margins (NIM) among U.S. banks from 1Q 2022 through 2Q 2026.

**Industry by the Numbers**

**Funding and Deposit Costs**

While costs tied to funding and deposits have steadily declined since their peaks in 3Q 2024, they are still far above their early 2022 levels when the Fed began its campaign of aggressively tightening interest rates.

Data from KFI shows that the average cost of total funding fell 36 bps to 1.87% for 2Q 2026, from the period high of 2.23% in 3Q 2024. Average cost of total deposits dropped 31 bps across the same period to 1.81% from the 3Q 2024 high of 2.12%. Average cost of interest-bearing deposits reached its peak in 4Q 2023 at 2.98% but fell the following quarter before rising once again to 2.66% in 3Q 2024. From there, the cost of interest-bearing deposits fell 40 bps to 2.26% in 2Q 2026.

Despite the relief banks have seen through easing deposit costs, the Fed’s 25-bp rate hike in September and consequent rate stay in October stand to reintroduce funding pressures and competition in the marketplace. Such competition among banks to retain or even grow deposits—especially the more consumer-enticing interest-bearing deposits—could see funding costs rise again.

**NIM**

Improvements in NIM for banks in five of the last six quarters hint at declining funding costs being a positive influence on bank profitability as opposed to primarily relying on strong performance from interest-earning assets.

Average NIM increased to 3.94% in 2Q 2026 from 3.51% in 3Q 2024, a 43-bp improvement, while earning-asset yields increased only modestly over the same period to 5.67% in 2Q 2026 from 5.60% in 3Q 2024.

Higher interest rates following the Fed’s rate hike could possibly have a mixed impact on banks depending on their exposure to certain assets. Those with floating rate loans and assets able to reprice in a short period of time would benefit from higher rates, while those allocated toward interest-bearing deposits would face renewed pressures.

**Non-Interest-Bearing Deposits**

Shares of non-interest-bearing deposits as a percentage of total deposits peaked in 3Q 2022 for banks at 26.91% but have noticeably fallen since then to 21.99% in 2Q 2026, a drop of roughly 5%.

This class of deposits is especially valuable for banks, as funds carrying no direct interest expense are prime for fueling the creation of loans and other interest-earning assets without the obligation to depositors. Shifts away from these deposits toward interest-bearing accounts due to market competition stand to increase funding costs and squeeze NIM, as banks with higher balances of non-interest-bearing deposits are vulnerable to repricing pressures.

title: US Dollar Index retests four-week lows, hammered by US midterm results
content_md:
TRENDING:

The US Dollar (USD) is showing the weakest performance among the major currencies on Wednesday, hammered by the US President Donald Trump’s and the Republican Party's defeat in the midterm election. The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the USD against six majors, is trading 0.6% lower on the day, with bears launching a fresh attack to the 101.25 support area at the time of writing.

The Democrats took control of the US Congress and the more disputed Senate in Tuesday's elections, which delivered a historic defeat to the Republican Party, which has lost historical strongholds like Texas, Kansas and North Carolina, where Republicans had held the government for decades.

Tech shares came under pressure after the election outcome. Concerns that Democrats will push for tougher regulation in the AI sector and stop most plans to build data centers provided a fresh blow to tech shares during the Asian session and boosted demand for the safe-haven government bonds. The yield of the 10-year note dropped a maximum of 10 pips following the election results, adding bearish pressure on the USD.

#### ING: Overnight price action provides a preview for markets in 2027

ING’s Chris Turner observes that the fact that the Democrats do not take office until January might have calmed investors and kept the US Dollar from falling further, but warns that “overnight price action could provide a preview for markets in 2027," as, in his opinion, "A Democratic Congress would be a mild dollar negative – both in terms of what it would mean for the AI story and the prospect of a prolonged US government shutdown."

Bearing this in mind, the ING Analysis Team sees US Dollar bears contained amid “a still-resilient US economy and at least one more rate hike from the Federal Reserve.”

In that sense, the US ADP Employment Change and the ISM Services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) will gather particular interest later in the day. The highlight of the week, however, will be Friday's Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report. Anything different from a strong labour market report next Friday might increase doubts about the US economic outlook and add pressure on the USD.

_(This story was corrected on November 4 at 13:49 GMT to correct the day of the week in the first paragraph, which is Wednesday instead of Thursday.)_

#### Economic Indicator

#### ADP Employment Change

The ADP Employment Change is a gauge of employment in the private sector released by the largest payroll processor in the US, Automatic Data Processing Inc. It measures the change in the number of people privately employed in the US. Generally speaking, a rise in the indicator has positive implications for consumer spending and is stimulative of economic growth. So a high reading is traditionally seen as bullish for the US Dollar (USD), while a low reading is seen as bearish.

**Next release:** Wed Nov 04, 2026 13:15

**Frequency:** Monthly

**Consensus:** 69K

**Previous:** 90K

**Source:** ADP Research Institute

#### Why it matters to traders?

Traders often consider employment figures from ADP, America’s largest payrolls provider, report as the harbinger of the Bureau of Labor Statistics release on Nonfarm Payrolls (usually published two days later), because of the correlation between the two. The overlaying of both series is quite high, but on individual months, the discrepancy can be substantial. Another reason FX traders follow this report is the same as with the NFP – a persistent vigorous growth in employment figures increases inflationary pressures, and with it, the likelihood that the Fed will raise interest rates. Actual figures beating consensus tend to be USD bullish.

#### ISM Services PMI

The Institute for Supply Management (ISM) Services Purchasing Managers Index (PMI), released on a monthly basis, is a leading indicator gauging business activity in the US services sector, which makes up most of the economy. The indicator is obtained from a survey of supply executives across the US based on information they have collected within their respective organizations. Survey responses reflect the change, if any, in the current month compared to the previous month. A reading above 50 indicates that the services economy is generally expanding, a bullish sign for the US Dollar (USD). A reading below 50 signals that services sector activity is generally declining, which is seen as bearish for USD.

**Next release:** Wed Nov 04, 2026 15:00

**Consensus:** 54.8

**Previous:** 54.9

**Source:** Institute for Supply Management

The Institute for Supply Management’s (ISM) Services Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) reveals the current conditions in the US service sector, which has historically been a large GDP contributor. A print above 50 shows expansion in the service sector’s economic activity. Stronger-than-expected readings usually help the USD gather strength against its rivals. In addition to the headline PMI, the Employment Index and the Prices Paid Index numbers are also watched closely by investors as they provide useful insights regarding the state of the labour market and inflation.

title: The U.S. Dollar Index fluctuates around 101.3; how will the weighting of political factors and policy trajectories change?
content_md:
- Headlines
- The U.S. Dollar Index fluctuates around 101.3; how will the weighting of political factors and policy trajectories change?

FX678 Finance· Nov 4 07:54

On Wednesday, November 4, with the U.S. midterm election results confirming that Democrats gained control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, the U.S. dollar index retreated to a low near 101.25. On October 28, the Federal Reserve kept the target range for the federal funds rate steady at 3.75% to 4%, with the committee maintaining a neutral tone regarding the pace of economic expansion, while inflationary pressures remained elevated.

#### The Impact of the U.S. Midterm Election Results on the U.S. Dollar

News that the Democratic Party has gained full control of both chambers triggered initial market concerns about policy continuity, putting downward pressure on the U.S. dollar index and short-term interest rates. Chris Turner, an analyst at ING Groep, noted that the election outcome's impact on the dollar is largely short-lived in terms of sentiment, with investors soon refocusing on economic growth data and the Federal Reserve's policy stance. As the new Congress will not officially take office until January next year and no substantive changes have yet occurred to the current policy framework, this time lag has prompted some position adjustments. Turner also pointed out that the U.S. president's acceptance of the election result has removed some expectations of downside risk, and overnight price action may serve as a reference point for the 2027 market. From a relative value perspective, the dollar's pricing against the euro, yen, and Swiss franc is driven more by interest rate spread expectations than by any single political narrative.

#### Expected Changes in AI Capital Expenditures and Market Sentiment Volatility

Given AI's role in driving economic growth, markets initially worried that the new U.S. Congress might affect related capital expenditure plans. Some Asian markets, heavily oriented toward chip exports, saw overnight declines of 3% to 4%, but subsequently recovered all losses. This volatility underscores investors' sensitivity to shifts in the regulatory environment, though actual policy changes still require confirmation through full legislative processes. Current trading dynamics are more focused on corporate capital expenditure data and earnings reports than on political expectations alone. Analysts believe the sustainability of AI-related investment hinges more on corporate cash flows and the pace of technological advancement, with noticeable lags in how political factors transmit through the system.

#### Fed Policy Stance and Short-Term Interest Rate Watch

At its October meeting, the Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged by a 10–2 vote, with two members voting against the hike. The committee described economic activity as maintaining a strong pace of expansion, while noting that inflation remains elevated and emphasizing the need for more data to confirm the future policy stance. Market pricing for the U.S. dollar is primarily viewed through the lenses of macroeconomic and monetary policy, with limited weight given to electoral factors. Turner stressed that it is not advisable to chase short-term dollar moves; macroeconomic and monetary policy trajectories remain the dominant drivers. With the federal funds rate held in the 3.75%–4% range, a relatively stable anchor has been provided for yield‑spread pricing.

#### U.S. Treasury Supply Schedule and Market Concerns

On the day, market attention focused on the U.S. Treasury's quarterly refunding schedule. Analysts expect the Treasury to continue seeking to reduce supply at the long end, making whether the short end can effectively absorb new issuance a key area of observation. Turner warned that volatility in the bond market could spill over to currency pairs such as USD/CHF, mirroring the market reaction seen in August. Current supply plans and cash‑flow conditions will determine the actual size of issuances and the mix of securities, with investors focusing on the specific maturity structure rather than the headline volume. The short‑end's rate‑setting capacity and shifts in the shape of the yield curve will directly affect the relative valuation of the dollar. From a financial‑logic perspective, supply adjustments influence exchange rates via term premia and spread channels, rather than acting as a simple directional driver.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

Question 1: Why did the results of the U.S. midterm elections fail to trigger a sustained decline in the U.S. dollar index?

A: With the new Congress set to take office in January next year and no substantial change in policy continuity, investors have swiftly refocused on economic growth data and the Federal Reserve's interest-rate trajectory, causing initial market jitters to subside.

Question 2: How do concerns about AI capital expenditures affect market pricing?

A: The market briefly worried that the new Congress might affect relevant investment plans, causing volatility in some chip-related markets, but prices subsequently rebounded, indicating that actual trading remains driven by fundamental data.

Question 3: What are the implications of the U.S. Treasury's refinancing program for short-term interest rates?

A: If the U.S. Treasury continues to adjust long-term supply and increase short-term issuance, the short-end interest rate tolerance will become a key observation point, potentially affecting the overall yield curve shape and the relative pricing of the U.S. dollar.

title: Democratic Congress Sweep Sends Global Stocks Lower as Dollar Falls
content_md:
A Democratic sweep of the US Congress sent global stocks lower on Wednesday as investors reassessed President Donald Trump's economic agenda. Asian technology shares suffered heavy losses, while the US dollar weakened and Treasury bonds gained. Meanwhile, Bitcoin fell below USD 76,000 as political uncertainty added pressure to already fragile financial markets.

The election results raised expectations of stronger congressional oversight of artificial intelligence, government spending, and financial regulation. Although Trump retains presidential veto powers, Democratic control of Congress could complicate his legislative priorities.

Asian technology stocks led the market decline as investors questioned whether greater political scrutiny could slow artificial intelligence investment. South Korea's Kospi dropped as much as 4%, while Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each lost more than 5%. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell nearly 5%, and Taiwan's benchmark declined 3.4%.

Meanwhile, Nasdaq 100 futures pointed to further weakness in US technology shares. Nvidia also declined in overnight trading, extending pressure across the semiconductor industry. Anna Wu, founder of Floodlines Research, warned that Democratic oversight could affect data-center construction, electricity consumption and local project approvals.

The political shift comes as investors already question the cost and potential returns of large-scale AI infrastructure projects.

Chris Weston, Pepperstone's head of research, said the scale of the Democratic victory had prompted investors to reconsider their exposure to risk.

Yet renewable energy companies moved in the opposite direction. Enphase Energy and SolarEdge gained as much as 12%, while First Solar rose 11% and Sunrun advanced 8.7%.

Investors anticipated that Democratic lawmakers could challenge some of Trump's restrictions on clean-energy development.

Treasury bonds also rallied as markets assessed whether Democratic control could limit Trump's tax cuts and spending proposals. Consequently, five-year Treasury yields dropped nine basis points to 4.68%, while the benchmark 10-year yield declined seven basis points to 4.89%.

Lower yields reflected expectations of reduced fiscal stimulus and potentially slower government borrowing. The answer depends partly on how Democratic lawmakers approach technology regulation, federal spending and the administration's remaining legislative priorities.

**Read More:** Democrats Near US Congress Majorities as Crypto Industry Faces Regulatory Uncertainty

Cryptocurrencies joined the broader market decline as investors questioned the future of industry-backed legislation. Bitcoin dropped as much as 2.8% to below USD 76,000. Ether and Solana also weakened as traders reduced exposure to riskier assets.

The decline followed existing pressure from spot Bitcoin ETF outflows and the aftermath of the reported Binance security breach. Trump had previously supported lighter cryptocurrency regulation, a strategic Bitcoin reserve and efforts to expand America's digital asset industry.

Meanwhile, Brent crude traded near USD 103 per barrel as renewed diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran eased immediate supply concerns. The decline offered some relief to energy-importing economies, including India. Nevertheless, uncertainty surrounding the conflict continued to affect oil markets.

Copper also fell as much as 1.5% as investors reassessed demand from AI infrastructure and the outlook for Trump's proposed tariffs. The metal's retreat followed concerns about future spending on data centers and power grids, alongside uncertainty over US trade policy.

The Democratic congressional sweep triggered losses across technology stocks, cryptocurrencies and the US dollar while supporting Treasury bonds and renewable energy shares. Investors now face uncertainty over AI investment, fiscal policy and cryptocurrency regulation. Congressional oversight, geopolitical developments and future spending decisions remain important factors for global markets.
