title: Euro zone inflation hits 4% for first time in three years as interest rate hike looms
content_md:
Inflation in the euro area jumped to a three-year high of 4% in October, a flash estimate showed on Wednesday.

The reading is in line with the expectations of economists polled by Reuters and was up from 3.8% in September.

Officials said the increase was largely due to surging energy costs, with energy inflation rising to 20.8% from 18.9% in September. Europe, a net energy importer, is vulnerable to external energy shocks and has seen prices rise steadily since the start of the Iran war.

October marked the first time inflation in the euro zone has hit or exceeded the 4% threshold since Sept. 2023's reading of 4.3%.

Inflation also varied across the 21 euro zone economies, with Lithuania recording the hottest inflation rate of 6.1% while Malta's was the lowest at 2.3%. All euro zone countries saw inflation hold above the European Central Bank's 2% target.

The euro was up 0.6% against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday morning, although the greenback fell against a basket of major currencies as counting continued in the U.S. midterm elections, while the yield on the 10-year German bund — broadly seen as a benchmark for euro zone bonds — was marginally higher.

Policymakers said underlying inflation and wages were broadly stable, despite inflation sitting at a three-year high.

The European Central Bank kept its key interest rate at 2.5% last month, following a hike of 25 basis points in September.

Shortly before Wednesday's inflation print, markets were pricing in a 71.8% chance of a hike at the ECB's final meeting of the year in December. Following the data release, markets were pricing in more than a 72% chance of rates rising.

Robert Mertens, global capital markets senior analyst at Validus Risk Management, cautioned that "ongoing turmoil in the French bond market is placing constraints on ECB policy" and the bank's capacity to get inflation under control.

"Should we see an easing in French political unrest, the ECB could potentially pursue a more aggressive hiking path," he said. "If the ECB can deploy more aggressive tightening relative to the Federal Reserve, we would see increased Euro support and upside versus the Dollar."

title: Global stocks rally, dollar dips after Democrats’ midterm sweep
content_md:
In a major setback to President Donald Trump, Democrats scored sweeping victories in Republican strongholds for the first time in generations.

The breadth of the party’s success was underscored by gains in districts long considered safely conservative, highlighting a political shift that may have caught some investors off guard.

“Democrats pulled off a double victory in the US midterm elections that few saw coming at the onset of the year. The blue wave means the federal government is sure to be divided on most issues,” Deborah Cunningham, chief investment officer, global liquidity markets at Federated Hermes, said.

“That typically creates a blockade against new legislation — an environment which broad financial markets traditionally view favourably as variables decrease.”

Opinion polls have shown Democratic voters favouring more control over AI, and investors expect the Democratic-controlled Congress to apply more scrutiny to the sector.

AI stocks in Asia initially led the decline in equity markets, while bonds and safe-haven currencies such as the Swiss franc gained.

By the time the bulk of the midterm results had filtered through in the European morning, equities had turned higher. MSCI’s All-World index was up 0.13%, while Europe’s STOXX 600 which has acted as a hedge against AI-related risks, was up 0.5%. US stock futures also ESc1, NQc1 edged into positive territory, having fallen by as much as 2% overnight.

Shares in Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX, which he intends to merge, were down around 4.5% to 5% on Europe’s Tradegate platform, compared with declines of around 0.3% to 0.9% for other Big Tech stocks.

“Overall, these results have had a mild impact on markets so far. Investors will move on from trading the uncertainty of the election results to trading the reality of what they mean for policy,” XTB research director Kathleen Brooks said.

“This is bad news for Tesla and SpaceX on Wednesday, but the semiconductor names, the backbone of the AI trade, could brush off concerns about AI regulation and continue to move higher after Tuesday’s stunning rally for the sector,” she said.

The AI boom has helped propel global markets in recent years, driven by heavy spending from tech giants racing to build data centres and expand computing capacity. That has made investors acutely sensitive to anything that could derail the technology’s rapid expansion.

The election outcome could also hold broad implications for the US fiscal outlook as well as sectors such as defence, healthcare and banking.

Futures on the small-cap Russell 2000 index RTYc1, which is more exposed to the US domestic economy, were last up 0.7%, having lost 1% earlier.

**Investors flock to safe havens**

Treasuries rallied as investors expect gridlock in Washington to cut government spending, with AI regulation also possibly slowing growth and reducing the need for rate hikes.

The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was down 3 basis points on the day at 4.92%, having fallen as much as 6 bps to a low of 4.89% overnight, which, in turn, weighed on the dollar.

“Bonds are coming out as the clear winner as markets put the AI trade on the chopping block and embrace the higher possibility that further tax cuts are put on ice and government spending slows,” Prashant Newnaha, senior rates strategist at TD Securities in Singapore, said.

In currencies, the dollar weakened broadly, leaving the euro up 0.4% at US$1.133 and the pound up 0.5% at US$1.348 GBP.

The yen and the Swiss franc, both safe-haven currencies, also notched up gains. The Swiss franc was the standout performer, with the dollar down 0.6% against it at 0.8163 francs. The dollar also fell 0.4% against the Japanese yen to 158.12.

In the oil market, prices were choppy on Wednesday after they hit a four-week low in the previous session as investors weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran against worries that recent attacks in both conflicts could further disrupt supplies. Brent crude LCOc1 was down 0.4% on the day at US$103.17 a barrel.

title: PM requests controlling inflation while pursuing double-digit growth
content_md:
**Hanoi (VNA)** – Prime Minister Le Minh Hung on November 4 reaffirmed the Government’s determination to achieve double-digit economic growth while maintaining macroeconomic stability and controlling inflation, stressing that inflation control must be given the highest priority in the final two months of 2026.

The PM made the statement while chairing the Government’s regular meeting to review socio-economic performance in October and the first 10 months of the year, and discuss key tasks and solutions for the remaining months.

According to reports presented at the meeting, Vietnam’s economy continued to record positive results across various sectors, with macroeconomic stability maintained and inflation kept under control. The consumer price index (CPI) rose 4.57% in the first 10 months, while state budget revenue reached nearly 2.45 quadrillion VND (95.2 billion USD), equivalent to 96.4% of the annual estimate.

Traditional growth drivers remained strong. Public investment disbursement reached 720.5 trillion VND, or 75.4% of the assigned plan. Foreign direct investment (FDI) attraction remained a bright spot, with registered capital totalling 54.85 billion USD and disbursed capital reaching 24.08 billion USD. Notably, total export-import turnover exceeded 1 trillion USD for the first time, reaching nearly 1.011 trillion USD.

Science and technology, innovation and digital transformation continued to be promoted as new growth drivers, while progress on major infrastructure projects was accelerated. Social welfare, cultural development, national defence, security and external relations also received due attention.

Concluding the meeting, PM Hung acknowledged the achievements while pointing out persistent difficulties and challenges. He noted that public investment disbursement remains low at several ministries, agencies, localities and key projects. The handling of long-standing projects and surplus public buildings and land in many localities have also failed to produce the expected results.

He called for more concrete measures to boost exports, reduce the trade deficit, stimulate private investment, remove obstacles facing businesses and improve productivity through science, technology and the development of new economic sectors. He also stressed the need to accelerate the development and completion of databases, connect information systems and simplify administrative procedures through the reuse of existing data.

The Government must also step up efforts to stimulate domestic consumption towards the year-end, while addressing issues related to healthcare, education, culture, employment, social welfare and people's living conditions, he stressed.

For November and the final two months of the year, the Government leader instructed ministries, sectors and localities to proactively develop action plans to implement resolutions and conclusions of the fourth plenum of the Party Central Committee. Ministries and agencies were also asked to work closely with National Assembly bodies to finalise draft laws and resolutions, ensuring consistency and effective institutionalisation of the Party’s guidelines, and prepare detailed documents for implementation to avoid delays once the legislation takes effect.

He instructed the steering committee for price management to work immediately with localities where CPI growth over the first 10 months exceeded the national average, particularly major cities, to devise appropriate measures to stabilise prices. Authorities must closely monitor the year-end growth scenario and implement measures to stimulate consumption and tourism, connect supply and demand, promote trade and organise trade fairs during the upcoming holiday and Lunar New Year period.

Regarding public investment, PM Hung called for reallocating capital from slow-moving projects to those with stronger disbursement capacity, aiming to achieve 100% disbursement of the assigned plan. He also urged stricter control over the number of projects, particularly the construction of administrative offices in provinces and cities, to prioritise resources for essential infrastructure and projects with widespread socio-economic impacts. Major projects must be accelerated, with particular attention paid to site clearance and construction material supplies. The 100-day plan to address bottlenecks in digital transformation must also be completed on schedule.

On social welfare, the Government leader directed the implementation of the plan based on the conclusions of General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and President To Lam regarding support for vulnerable groups. Priorities include accelerating the search for, recovery and identification of fallen soldiers’ remains, meeting the 2026 targets for social housing and rental housing, and ensuring progress in building inter-level boarding schools in border communes.

The Prime Minister assigned specific tasks to ministries to ensure coordinated implementation. The Ministry of Finance was asked to closely monitor price developments, update inflation scenarios and propose appropriate price management measures, while accelerating reforms in value-added tax and tax administration.

The State Bank of Vietnam was urged to proactively and flexibly manage the monetary policy to stabilise the value of the Vietnamese currency, interest rates and exchange rates, and create more favourable lending conditions for production, business, priority sectors and small- and medium-sized enterprises. It must also strengthen supervision to ensure the banking system safety. The Ministry of Industry and Trade was tasked with ensuring stable supplies of essential goods, particularly petroleum and electricity, accelerating adjustments to the Power Development Plan VIII and completing the draft decree on petroleum trading in November. It was also instructed to promote exports, control the trade deficit, diversify markets, make effective use of free trade agreements and step up negotiations on a reciprocal trade agreement with the US.

Meanwhile, the Ministry of Construction must closely monitor prices of building materials, housing and transport services, while coordinating with localities to remove obstacles and accelerate major infrastructure projects. The Ministry of Agriculture and Environment was asked to ensure stable supplies of essential food and agricultural products, balance domestic consumption and exports, and reorganise agricultural supply and distribution networks.

PM Hung also called for stronger application of strategic technologies, improvements in education and healthcare services, year-end tourism stimulus measures and the development of special policies to attract and retain talented people.

He assigned the Ministry of National Defence, the Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to strengthen strategic policy research and advice, and accelerate key projects in national defence and security.

The Prime Minister urged Deputy Prime Ministers and Government members to proactively implement their assigned tasks and contribute directly to the draft National Assembly resolution on the 2027 socio-economic situation, and continue working to ensure that key targets and tasks for the remaining months of 2026 are fulfilled./.

title: U.S. Dollar Index Lowest in Five Weeks, Markets Worry Democrats Take Control of Congress
content_md:
JAKARTA - The US dollar index (USD) fell to its lowest level in five weeks, following the Democratic Party's big victory in the midterm elections. Investors are worried about the possibility of Democrats taking control of Congress and limiting President Donald Trump's room to maneuver in carrying out his economic agenda.

According to the Anadolu Agency report, quoted, Wednesday, November 4, the US dollar index fell below 101.5, its lowest position in five weeks. This index measures the strength of the dollar against a number of major world currencies.

The weakening occurred when market participants took note of the election results which opened the opportunity for the Democratic Party to control both chambers of the US Congress, namely the Senate and the House of Representatives (DPR).

If Democrats control both, the discussion of the law has the potential to be deadlocked due to differences in political attitudes with the Trump administration.

The condition can also hinder the US President's economic agenda and limit federal government spending.

The Democrats' sweeping victory also has the potential to pave the way for stricter rules on artificial intelligence (AI).

In addition, supervision of companies is expected to increase. The tightening of AI rules and corporate supervision are feared to dampen the US economic growth projection.

Beyond the election results, investors are also looking at the possibility of the United States launching a military operation against Iran.

The risk is of concern as diplomatic negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain at an impasse.

title: Giá điện giảm 2% từ 1/11, EVN công bố mức tiết kiệm hàng tháng của người dân và doanh nghiệp
description: Theo tính toán của EVN, có hộ gia đình được giảm gần 78.000 đồng tiền điện mỗi tháng, trong khi tổng chi phí điện của các nhóm khách hàng dự kiến giảm hơn 1.500 tỷ đồng.
content_md:
Theo tính toán của EVN, có hộ gia đình được giảm gần 78.000 đồng tiền điện mỗi tháng, trong khi tổng chi phí điện của các nhóm khách hàng dự kiến giảm hơn 1.500 tỷ đồng.

Ngày 4/11, Tập đoàn Điện lực Việt Nam (EVN) công bố bảng tính chi tiết tác động của việc giảm 2% giá bán lẻ điện bình quân, kết hợp áp dụng biểu giá điện sinh hoạt mới từ ngày 1/11/2026.

Theo đó, giá bán lẻ điện bình quân giảm xuống còn 2.159,9 đồng/kWh, chưa bao gồm VAT. Biểu giá điện sinh hoạt cũng được rút gọn từ 6 bậc xuống 5 bậc.

Đối với hộ gia đình, EVN tính toán hộ sử dụng 100 kWh/tháng được giảm 11.600 đồng, hộ dùng 200 kWh giảm 20.700 đồng và hộ dùng 300 kWh giảm khoảng 31.100 đồng.

Mức giảm đáng kể hơn ở nhóm sử dụng 400–700 kWh/tháng, dao động từ 76.700 đến 77.900 đồng. Trong đó, hộ dùng 700 kWh được giảm 77.900 đồng, cao nhất trong các mức tiêu thụ được EVN đưa ra.

Ở mức 800 kWh, tiền điện giảm 39.500 đồng, còn mức 900 kWh chỉ giảm 1.100 đồng. Ngược lại, hộ dùng 1.000 kWh phải trả thêm 37.300 đồng và hộ dùng 2.000 kWh tăng 421.300 đồng/tháng.

Theo EVN, khoảng 98,23% hộ sử dụng điện sinh hoạt được giảm tiền điện, trong khi 1,77% số hộ thuộc nhóm tiêu thụ cao có tiền điện tăng.

Đối với doanh nghiệp và các nhóm khách hàng khác, tổng chi phí mua điện dự kiến giảm 1.531,89 tỷ đồng mỗi tháng.

Trong đó, nhóm khách hàng sản xuất được giảm nhiều nhất với 578,15 tỷ đồng/tháng, tiếp đến là kinh doanh dịch vụ với 433,02 tỷ đồng và khách hàng sinh hoạt với 424,13 tỷ đồng.

Đáng chú ý, riêng các cơ sở lưu trú du lịch dự kiến giảm 342,63 tỷ đồng tiền điện mỗi tháng, trong khi các trạm sạc xe điện giảm khoảng 53,38 tỷ đồng. Nhóm hành chính sự nghiệp và bán buôn điện lần lượt được giảm 47,04 tỷ đồng và 49,54 tỷ đồng.

Ở chiều ngược lại, Phó Tổng Giám đốc EVN Nguyễn Đình Phước cho biết việc điều chỉnh giá điện dự kiến khiến doanh thu tập đoàn giảm gần 1.600 tỷ đồng mỗi tháng. Dù vậy, EVN vẫn phấn đấu đạt và vượt các chỉ tiêu tài chính năm 2026 được giao.

title: Banks provide support to businesses in Khanh Hoa.
content_md:
**Bank capital provides support for businesses.**

From a small-scale seafood purchasing business that frequently faced capital difficulties, Tuan Cong Co., Ltd. in Nam Nha Trang ward (Khanh Hoa province) has gradually developed into an enterprise with annual revenue of tens of billions of VND. Behind this journey, besides the dynamism and efforts of the business owner, there is also the persistent support of bank credit.

Recalling the early days of her business, Ms. Tran Thi Cong, Director of Tuan Cong Co., Ltd., said that the company mainly purchased seafood from fishermen in localities south of Nha Trang, then supplied it to seafood processing businesses in the area. However, limited capital caused the business to face difficulties at many times, especially when the demand for seafood increased.

The turning point came in 2009, when the facility established a credit relationship with Agribank's Khanh Hoa branch. The timely addition of capital enabled the facility to proactively procure raw materials, expand its market, and gradually develop into a business. To date, Tuan Cong Co., Ltd. maintains annual revenue of tens of billions of VND, providing regular employment for 11 local workers.

According to Ms. Cong, the bank's support throughout the operation process has helped the business overcome initial obstacles, gradually stabilize, and expand. In particular, maintaining long-term credit relationships allows the business to be more proactive in capital planning and seize market opportunities.

|  |
| Unlocking credit flows contributes to creating momentum for many businesses in Khanh Hoa. |

Ms. Lam Thi Hong, Deputy Director of Agribank's Khanh Hoa Provincial Branch, said that in recent times, the branch has focused on expanding credit investment and developing banking products and services to serve the agricultural and rural sectors, as well as the local business community. Along with ensuring safe and effective credit growth, the bank facilitates customers' access to capital, expands production and business, thereby contributing to job creation and increased income for workers.

Not only in the field of seafood production and trade, bank capital also contributes to promoting the transformation of agricultural production methods and the development of collective economic activities in many localities.

In Phuoc Dinh commune, Tuan Tu General Service Cooperative is one of the typical collective economic models of the Cham people. From small, individual households lacking capital, the members have gradually linked up to develop the green asparagus growing area towards commercial production, linked to the consumer market.

Currently, the cooperative has 85 members, with no members classified as poor or near-poor households. On average, the cooperative purchases 150-300 kg of green asparagus from its members daily. Through its linkages with businesses, the products of member households have a more stable market, contributing to improved income and sustainable livelihood development.

|  |
| Tuan Tu General Services Cooperative (Khanh Hoa) is currently being approached by the banking sector. |

Mr. Lo Trung Tai, Deputy Director of Tuan Tu General Service Cooperative, shared that capital from Agribank Ninh Phuoc Branch has helped many households realize their desire to develop clean agriculture right in their hometown. Currently, the cooperative's outstanding loan at Agribank is approximately 5 billion VND. In particular, the bank's shortened project appraisal and loan application processing time has facilitated the cooperative's timely allocation of resources for production investment.

**Strengthening connectivity and facilitating access to credit.**

To meet the capital needs for economic development, the banking system in Khanh Hoa province continues to expand its financial service offerings. Currently, the province has 53 bank branches, 157 transaction offices, 7 people's credit funds, 422 ATMs, and 5,118 POS machines. Agribank alone has added 17 second-level branches; Agribank and the Social Policy Bank also maintain transaction points down to the commune level, facilitating access to banking services for people and businesses.

According to a representative of the State Bank of Vietnam's Regional Branch 10, in recent times, credit institutions in the area have actively implemented solutions to increase credit growth, prioritizing capital for production, business, and other drivers of economic growth. The bank-business connection activities continue to be emphasized to understand needs, address difficulties, and improve customers' access to capital.

By October 31, 2026, capital mobilization by credit institutions in Khanh Hoa province is estimated to reach VND 209,425 billion, an increase of 13% compared to the beginning of the year. Outstanding loans are estimated at VND 211,232 billion, an increase of VND 7,909 billion, equivalent to a 3.89% increase compared to the beginning of the year and a 6.05% increase compared to the same period last year.

|  |
| Unlocking credit flows will create momentum for businesses in Khanh Hoa to develop. |

These figures show that the scale of bank capital continues to expand, meeting the credit needs of people and businesses. However, in the context of businesses still facing pressure from costs, consumer markets, and the need to innovate production methods, improving the efficiency of connections and delivering capital to those in need remains a crucial task…

Mr. Vo Van Thanh, Deputy Director of the State Bank of Vietnam's Regional Branch 10, said that in the coming time, the unit will continue to closely monitor the socio-economic situation, banking activities, and capital needs in key economic sectors. Based on this, it will proactively advise local Party committees and authorities to coordinate the implementation of credit programs and policies that are appropriate to the practical situation.

In particular, the State Bank of Vietnam's Regional Branch 10 will continue to direct and promote the bank-enterprise connection program, promptly identifying and resolving difficulties and obstacles in credit activities. At the same time, it will monitor interest rate developments and encourage credit institutions to reduce operating costs to create conditions for lowering lending interest rates, supporting people and businesses.

In addition, credit institutions in the area are also required to strengthen the application of information technology, promote digital transformation, and publicly disclose lending interest rates; review and simplify documents and procedures, and diversify credit products to suit actual needs. Facilitating customers' access to capital must be linked to ensuring operational safety, complying with legal regulations, and not relaxing credit granting conditions, thereby controlling risks and limiting the 발생 of bad debts.

title: Focus efforts on boosting growth in the final months of the year.
content_md:
Determined to achieve its 11% growth target in 2026, the province is implementing a comprehensive set of solutions to unlock resources, create leverage to boost production and business, and achieve a strong breakthrough in the final sprint of the year.

Contractors are accelerating infrastructure construction at Song Lo 2 Industrial Park, creating clean land to welcome FDI inflows.

At the end of the third quarter of 2026, the province's GRDP increased by 10.01% compared to the same period last year. This is a positive result, placing Phu Tho second among the nine provinces in the Northern Midlands and Mountains region, and eleventh among the 34 provinces and cities nationwide. Contributing to this growth picture, the industrial and construction sector continued to affirm its leading role with a growth rate of 13.48%. The service sector increased by 8.66%; agriculture, forestry, and fisheries maintained stable growth at 3.61%. The total GRDP of the province at current prices is estimated at VND 345.4 trillion, an increase of VND 44.9 trillion compared to the same period last year, demonstrating an economy operating in the right direction and with strong internal potential. In particular, the total investment implemented in the province reached VND 118.4 trillion, an increase of 15.8%, reflecting the strong confidence of investors in the business environment in Phu Tho. The economic picture for the first nine months of 2026 is creating a solid foundation for Phu Tho to confidently accelerate in the final stretch. However, the breakthrough period in the remaining months of the year is predicted to face considerable pressure. In fact, the growth rate of industrial production is trending slower compared to the early months of the year due to high input material prices and a shrinking market for some key products. The sharp decline in registered capital in the domestic direct investment (DDI) sector also presents a challenge requiring decisive solutions.

To realize the target of 11% growth for the whole year, the Provincial Steering Committee for Double-Digit Economic Growth has activated a high-intensity operational mode, focusing on identifying bottlenecks to unlock resources. First and foremost, for the "locomotive" of industry, the province has set a top priority on continuing to closely support high-tech processing and manufacturing industries. This is the main driving force, as the electronics, computer, and optical product manufacturing sectors have continuously surged thanks to stable orders from global corporations. The province is also focusing on removing procedural obstacles and creating favorable conditions for new-generation projects to quickly become operational, thereby increasing sustainable new production capacity for the locality.

Along with maintaining the pace of industrial production, the province has identified the disbursement of public investment capital as a key driver to boost growth and create a ripple effect. To unlock the remaining large amount of capital in the last two months of the year, the province is decisively directing the removal of bottlenecks in land clearance for key projects using a phased approach, emphasizing the responsibility of the heads of departments. By the end of October 2026, the entire province had disbursed over 12,400 billion VND, reaching approximately 60% of the plan assigned by the Prime Minister. Currently, the compensation process for inter-regional transport infrastructure projects, industrial park infrastructure, and the key national railway line from Lao Cai to Hanoi and Hai Phong passing through the province is being strictly monitored week by week to ensure clean land for construction. Simultaneously, FDI inflows continue to be seen as a strategic lever for growth. From the beginning of the year until now, the province has attracted $2.7 billion in investment, an 84% increase compared to the same period last year and reaching 153.7% of the annual plan. To maintain this attractiveness, along with efforts to improve the investment environment, bank credit flows are also being oriented to closely follow the real economic flow, focusing on production and business with a total outstanding loan balance of over 400 trillion VND. Notably, FDI enterprises have the highest loan growth rate, reaching 41.7%, demonstrating the harmonious alignment between local monetary policy and investment flows. Another inseparable key element in the growth scenario is stimulating domestic consumption and facilitating trade. Currently, the service and trade sector in the province continues to maintain double-digit growth compared to the same period last year. To maintain this momentum, the province proactively regulates the market, ensuring a smooth supply of goods, while also promoting travel, accommodation, and culinary services to maximize consumer spending potential during the year-end period.

From consistent practice, Phu Tho 's economic management mindset has undergone a clear shift, no longer relying on traditional resources such as land and cheap labor. Instead, the province is determined to minimize investment approval times, tighten administrative discipline, and thoroughly eliminate the tendency of officials to shirk responsibility and avoid accountability. With a spirit of decisive action, a genuine commitment to supporting businesses, and a mechanism for tracking results on a weekly and monthly basis, Phu Tho is confidently transforming growth pressure into a powerful internal driving force, aiming for successful breakthroughs.

Tran Tinh

title: Dollar Index Drops to Five-Week Low as Democrats Make Election Gains
content_md:
Financial markets were assessing the possibility that Democrats could take control of both chambers of Congress, a development that could create legislative deadlock and restrict President Donald Trump's ability to implement his economic policies.

Investors also considered the potential implications for federal spending, with expectations that a shift in congressional control could limit government expenditures and complicate efforts to advance the administration's economic agenda.

A Democratic victory in both chambers could also influence the regulatory environment, potentially opening the way for tighter rules governing artificial intelligence (AI) and more extensive oversight of corporate activities. Such developments could affect business confidence and weigh on expectations for broader economic growth.

Beyond domestic political developments, currency markets remained sensitive to geopolitical risks, particularly the possibility of renewed US military action against Iran following the elections.

Diplomatic negotiations between Washington and Tehran remained stalled, adding to uncertainty over the direction of relations between the two countries and the potential consequences for regional stability.

title: Dollar, Global Stocks Fall as Democrats Sweep U.S. Midterms
content_md:
The dollar and global stock markets fell as Democrats were projected to win sweeping majorities in both chambers of the U.S. Congress in the midterm elections, raising concerns that the buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure, a key driver of economic growth, could slow.

According to the Financial Times on the 4th local time, vote counting from the U.S. midterm elections held on the 3rd Eastern time showed Democrats were likely to secure majorities in both the Senate and the House of Representatives.

Futures on the technology-heavy Nasdaq 100 index fell 2.1% at the New York market open, while S&P 500 futures dropped 1.2%. Futures on Europe's Stoxx 600 index declined 1.3%. Asian markets, closely tied to demand for AI chips, also tumbled. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 4.5% to its lowest level since May, and South Korea's KOSPI lost 3.4%. The U.S. dollar index fell as much as 0.61% to its weakest level in more than a month.

If Democrats take control of Congress, the result would create a divided government alongside the administration of President Donald Trump, who remains in office. A divided government refers to a situation in which the president's party differs from the majority party in the legislature. Such an arrangement typically produces gridlock in Washington, limiting policy changes and generally benefiting financial markets. But the swings in stocks and the dollar in this election reflect concerns that Democrats could put the brakes on the AI industry, viewed as a core engine of economic growth, the FT reported.

Investors had been focused on the outcomes of the governor's races in Texas and Ohio. Governors oversee zoning designations and permits for data center construction and can order projects halted, giving them a critical role in whether such developments proceed.

Texas is a central hub that hosts about a quarter of the U.S. data centers expected to be operating by 2030, and it is also where the Encinal combined-cycle gas power plant project is being built, the first strategic investment project in the United States selected by the South Korean government. Ohio is counted among the five largest data center hubs in the United States.

Democrats won decisively in both states. Democratic candidates prevailed in Senate and gubernatorial races in Texas, where no Democrat had won a statewide election since 1994, as well as in Ohio, which had been seen as a battleground.

Robert Tipp, head of global bonds at PGIM, said the effect of the election could be seen in the decline in the Nasdaq and in interest rates, adding that the market reacted immediately because the rapid growth of the AI industry is putting considerable pressure on the supply side.

Priya Misra, a portfolio manager at J.P. Morgan Asset Management, said she was concerned the election results would weigh on the stock market, noting that pushback against data centers is spreading on a bipartisan basis and that the economy and equity markets depend heavily on AI.

title: Oil Prices Rebound as Middle East Supply Fears Return
content_md:
Crude oil prices, which fell to their lowest in four weeks, staged a rebound earlier today, as traders shifted their attention from the U.S. midterms to the Middle East, awaiting the next step in the war.

Benchmarks dropped sharply on Tuesday on reports that Iran may be open to discussions on previously non-negotiable issues, but at the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $103.60 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $95.98 per barrel, after two energy consultancies warned against too much Gulf oil supply rebound optimism.

Rystad Energy said yesterday it did not expect crude oil flows out of the Persian Gulf to return to normal anytime soon, even if the United States and Iran reach some form of agreement that would end the war. Noting some of the priorities for the U.S., the firm said: “We consider it unlikely that all these points of contention can be resolved within the coming year.”

Vortexa, meanwhile, said October oil flows via the Strait of Hormuz were lower than the previous month’s, countering a string of reports saying oil exports from the Gulf were back to pre-war levels, and even exceeding them. According to the firm’s data, combined exports of crude oil, condensates, and fuels averaged 17.1 million barrels daily last month. That was down from 18.9 million barrels in total daily exports in September.

Meanwhile, “President Trump's conflicting signals, with military strikes continuing alongside statements downplaying further escalation, have made it difficult for traders to build strong directional conviction,” Phillip Nova analyst Priyanka Sachdeva said as quoted by Reuters.

“The market still has a large risk premium baked in, particularly given the strong oil flows from the Persian Gulf,” ING’s commodity team said in a note on Tuesday, adding that despite recent positive signals from both the U.S. and Iran, it was too early to get optimistic about the end of the war.

title: Gold prices hit $4,000 as Democrats see electoral Sweep to gain control of Congress
content_md:
(Kitco News) - The gold market is seeing a healthy rally as the Democratic Party appears poised to take control of Congress following significant electoral gains in both the House and Senate.

Spot gold is testing initial resistance at $4,000 an ounce, up nearly 2% on the session, as political pundits begin making their final calls on the 2026 midterm elections. As results continue to come in, analysts note that a Democratic sweep could lay the groundwork for higher gold prices through 2027.

In an interview with Kitco News, Christopher Vecchio, Head of Futures and Forex Strategy at Tastylive, said that a Democratic sweep could create a favorable environment for gold heading into the new year, particularly if political uncertainty accelerates an economic slowdown.

Vecchio explained that Democratic control of Congress could create headwinds for the technology sector, particularly the massive investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure and data centers that has supported economic growth.

He noted that a slowdown in data center construction could trigger a broader decline in business investment over the next three to six months, potentially weakening the economy enough to change the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook.

"So I'm painting a picture here, right? Midterm elections are done. Democrats sweep. The market becomes fearful that the data center build-out's gonna slow down," he said. "Business investment declines. Fed doesn't have to hike. That's gonna put real yields in a really tough spot. They're probably heading lower.”

Lower real yields and a weaker U.S. dollar reduces the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold, potentially allowing the precious metal to regain its lost momentum.

Although Vecchio acknowledged that gold has struggled to attract safe-haven demand during the recent equity market selloff, he expects the precious metal to become more resilient and potentially benefit from the election results through the first quarter of 2027.

However, he cautioned that Democratic control of Congress would not immediately reduce geopolitical uncertainty, particularly surrounding the ongoing conflict with Iran. The new Congress will not take office until January, leaving President Donald Trump with a window to pursue additional policy initiatives.

Beyond the immediate political reaction, other analysts argue that gold's long-term investment appeal remains tied to America's deteriorating fiscal position, regardless of which party controls Congress.

Jen Bawden, Founder of Bawden Capital, said that while the election could create short-term volatility in the U.S. dollar and bond yields, neither political party has offered a convincing solution to the country's mounting debt burden.

Bawden explained that persistent fiscal deficits and rising debt-servicing costs will continue to pressure the U.S. economy, potentially forcing the Federal Reserve to eventually ease monetary policy or expand its balance sheet.

"For me, gold is a hedge against the risk that policymakers respond to mounting debt with easy money, weakening the dollar's purchasing power over time," she said.

Although Bawden sees gold benefiting from these longer-term fiscal risks, she cautioned that a stronger U.S. dollar and elevated interest rates could continue to weigh on prices.

"The election matters because policy matters. But the longer concern is whether either party can restore confidence in America's finances. Gold's appeal rests on that uncertainty, whichever party wins control of Congress," she said.

Chris Weston, Head of Research at Pepperstone, also sees the potential for a Democratic sweep to create a supportive environment for gold, but said the size of the party's congressional majority could prove more important than the election victory itself.

Weston noted that gold has already attracted renewed buying interest as the U.S. dollar weakens and both nominal and real Treasury yields decline.

He explained that a commanding Democratic majority could constrain Trump's domestic legislative agenda, potentially prompting the administration to pursue a more aggressive international policy.

“The combination of a weaker USD, falling real yields and demand for protection against a potentially more unpredictable and confrontational Trump administration looks to be providing a compelling backdrop for gold buyers," he said.

However, despite the potential for a more favorable political and monetary environment, one veteran market strategist warns that gold's recent price action suggests its long-term bullish trend may already be broken.

In an interview with Kitco News, Michele Schneider, Chief Market Strategist at MarketGauge, said that although a Democratic sweep could eventually support gold prices, investors should not assume the precious metal will automatically benefit from political uncertainty or falling interest rates.

"The flight to safety in gold has been broken," she said.

Schneider noted that the fundamental arguments supporting gold's historic rally have not disappeared. Government debt continues to rise, inflation remains elevated and geopolitical uncertainty persists. However, these factors have failed to generate renewed investment demand.

Instead, she sees growing evidence that investors are turning to U.S. Treasury bonds for protection as yields decline.

"Gold doesn't seem to be the big flight to safety," she said. "And now, all of a sudden, bonds are."

Schneider acknowledged that continued central bank purchases could help restore investor confidence, particularly if foreign governments remain concerned about U.S. debt and the long-term purchasing power of fiat currencies.

Under that scenario, gold would need to reclaim $4,000 an ounce to generate renewed bullish momentum.

However, she warned that the downside risks remain significant. A break below support around $3,940 could trigger another wave of selling, potentially pushing prices toward $3,500 an ounce and eventually as low as $2,500.

title: US Dollar Index dips to late September lows as Democrats gain edge
content_md:
TRENDING:

The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, comes under intense selling pressure during the Asian session on Wednesday, dropping to its lowest level since late September as early US midterm election results heightened political uncertainty. In fact, the initial trend shows the possibility of Democrats securing control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. This raises the prospect of gridlock in Washington, which could limit government spending.

Meanwhile, a Democratic sweep could be potentially negative for tech stocks and economic growth, boosting demand for safe-haven assets and triggering a fresh leg down in US bond yields. This turns out to be another factor that contributes to the DXY's intraday slump to the 101.25 area. However, hawkish US Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations, along with persistent geopolitical uncertainties, offer some support to the Greenback and help limit deeper losses, warranting some caution for aggressive bearish traders.

According to the EMC Group's FedWatch Tool, traders are currently pricing in over a 75% chance that the US central bank will raise borrowing costs again in December. The bets were reaffirmed by the Labor Department’s monthly Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, or JOLTS report, on Tuesday, which showed that job openings rose more than expected in September to 7.5 million. This solidifies bets for an imminent Fed rate hike against the backdrop of resilient economic growth and persistent price pressures.

Meanwhile, President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the US has no immediate plans to strike Iran, defying Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's hint at an attack later this week. However, the geopolitical risk premium remains in play as a senior Iranian official told Reuters that the Strait of Hormuz will reopen only if sanctions are waived, and the US naval blockade ends. Furthermore, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said that four tankers were destroyed after striking mines south of the Strait of Hormuz.

Investors, however, remain hopeful about a potential diplomatic resolution to end the US-Iran war. Moving ahead, Wednesday's US economic docket features the release of the ADP report on private-sector employment and ISM Services PMI. Apart from this, the incoming geopolitical headlines could provide some impetus to the DXY. The focus, however, remains glued to the closely watched US monthly employment details, popularly known as the Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report, due on Friday.

#### DXY 4-hour chart

#### Technical Analysis

The DXY maintains a bearish near-term bias following an intraday break below the 200-period Simple Moving Average (SMA) on the 4-hour chart. However, some follow-through weakness below the first support near the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement at 101.26 is needed to back the case for further losses to 100.75 and 100.24,.

Moreover, broader structural support emerge toward 99.51 and 98.59 if selling pressure resumes. On the topside, initial resistance is seen at the 200-period SMA at 101.71, followed higher by the 23.6% retracement at 101.89 and then the recent cycle anchor near 102.92.

#### US midterm elections FAQs

#### What are the US midterm elections?

The US midterm elections are the federal elections held halfway through a president's four-year term. Voters choose all 435 members of the House of Representatives, about one-third of the Senate, and, in many states, governors and other state and local officials.

#### When are the 2026 midterm elections?

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Federal law sets it as the Tuesday after the first Monday in November. Early voting and mail voting are already under way in many states.

#### Why are the US midterm elections important?

They decide which party controls each chamber of Congress for the last two years of President Donald Trump's term. The majority party sets the legislative agenda, chooses committee leaders and, in the Senate, controls confirmations of judges and senior officials.

#### Is the president on the ballot in the 2026 midterm elections?

No. The president is elected every four years; the next presidential election is in November 2028. Midterms are often seen as a referendum on the sitting president's party, which historically tends to lose House seats.

#### How could the 2026 midterm elections affect the US dollar?

Most analysts expect a modest, short-lived reaction in the US Dollar rather than a lasting trend. A divided Congress is widely seen as the base case and is partly priced in. Treasury yields may react more noticeably to the results. Outcomes that raise expectations of fiscal stimulus tend to lift yields and the US Dollar, while gridlock that limits new spending can pull both lower. Political friction, such as funding or debt-ceiling standoffs, can also briefly lift the Dollar as a safe haven. Over six to twelve months, growth and Federal Reserve policy matter more than the vote.

#### How do stocks usually perform around midterm elections?

US stocks have historically been weak before midterms and strong after them. Since 1950, the S&P 500 has been higher 12 months after every midterm election, 19 out of 19, with an average gain of about 15%. Analysts link the pattern to uncertainty fading once results are known. Past performance does not guarantee future returns, and some strategists note that high valuations in 2026 could test the streak.

#### Is a divided Congress good for markets?

Markets have often welcomed a divided government because gridlock makes sweeping changes to taxes, spending and regulation less likely. Under a Republican president, the S&P 500 has historically done well in years following midterms that split control of Congress. The risks are funding deadlines, debt-ceiling fights and congressional investigations, which can add short-term volatility.

title: Danish footwear maker ECCO halts Vietnam factory operations
content_md:
| Photo: Obayashi Vietnam |

The factory, located in Bau Bang Industrial Park in Ho Chi Minh City, halted production on November 2, according to Ho Chi Minh City Export Processing Zones and Industrial Parks Management Board. The company employs 1,611 people, including 259 outsourced workers.

The move is part of ECCO Group's global restructuring strategy to reduce costs amid a challenging economic environment. After years of declining demand and significant overcapacity, the group aims to concentrate production at a few existing plants, with a focus on expanding its headquarters in Denmark and other existing factories to achieve long-term sustainability.

A small number of employees will remain over the next few months to assist with completing the dissolution process in accordance with regulations. They will be informed of their subsequent working arrangements. The employment contracts of most employees will be terminated on November 30.

Established in Denmark in 1963, ECCO is a footwear brand with manufacturing operations in Vietnam.

Construction of the Bau Bang footwear factory began in October 2019 across 120,000 square metres, with registered investment capital of $38.18 million. The facility commenced operations in April 2020.

As reported by *Women's Wear Daily*, ECCO has also decided to cease operations at its Portugal factory, which has about 650 workers. The Danish shoemaker's global restructuring also includes about 400 additional positions that will be lost across global and regional functions.

ECCO has been under pressure over the years. All sales channels experienced declining sales, most profoundly in its own operated direct-to-consumer business.

title: Asian FX gains as dollar falls on U.S. midterm results, yuan weakens on PBOC move
content_md:
Investing.com -- The U.S. dollar fell to its lowest level in over a month on Wednesday, as currency market participants digested a Democratic sweep in the U.S. midterm elections and weighed potential policy ramifications that could possibly dent economic growth.

Watchers of monetary policy also received some mixed economic data ahead of Friday's all-important U.S. nonfarm payrolls report.

At 14:21 ET (19:21 GMT), the U.S. dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of six major peers, fell 0.3% to 101.55. The gauge earlier hit a session low at 101.10, its lowest since September 30.

#### **Democrats seize control of both chambers of Congress**

Figures from the Associated Press showed the Democrats securing a majority in both the Senate and the House of Representatives, even with some votes still yet to be counted.

In the 100-seat Senate, Democrats have won 54 seats, with two races still to be called, according to AP projections. Democrats have also seized 228 seats in the House of Representatives, surpassing the 218-seat threshold needed to have a majority in the lower chamber.

Notable Democratic victories included James Talarico taking winning in a Senate race in the traditional Republican stronghold of Texas, along with Abdul El-Sayed emerging victorious in a Senate race in the key swing state of Michigan. The Democrats flipped at least seven seats from the Republicans in the Senate.

The outcome represents a sharp repudiation of the first two years of President Donald Trump's second term, a time during which Republicans held slim majorities in the House and Senate. At least some Democratic approval will now be required for legislation to pass through Congress from January, although Trump will retain his ability to veto bills without the threat of a Congressional override.

The immediate consequences of the results could be stricter regulation at the federal and local level of artificial intelligence-related investments such as the construction of data centers. Given that AI infrastructure buildouts have boosted the U.S. economy, any hit to it could affect growth and take the shine off the world's premier currency.

"The most important policy implication of a Democratic landslide in the U.S. midterm election is a prospective slowdown of data center construction. And insofar as the AI-driven infrastructure investment cycle has supported growth in the U.S., especially, any politically-driven slowdown would be adverse for the USD. This is among the three most important factors driving the value of the USD in FX markets in the medium term, along with oil/war and European debt sustainability," Thierry Wizman, global FX and rates strategist at Macquarie, said.

title: Chinese yuan hits over two-week low against dollar as PBOC signals caution on appreciation
content_md:
The onshore yuan fell to 6.6832 per dollar in early trading, its weakest level since October 19, before recovering slightly to 6.6794 as of 0303 GMT. The offshore yuan also declined, trading at 6.6782 per dollar, down around 0.13% during Asian trade.

The weakness followed the People's Bank of China's (PBOC) decision on Tuesday to raise the foreign exchange reserve requirement ratio by 2 percentage points to 6% from 4%. The move is aimed at limiting the supply of foreign currency in the domestic market and slowing the yuan's appreciation.

The decision marks one of Beijing's strongest attempts yet to rein in the currency's rally, which has seen it appreciate around 5% against the dollar so far this year.

The PBOC set its daily midpoint rate at 6.7180 per dollar on Wednesday, the weakest level since October 23. The fixing was 369 pips weaker than the Reuters estimate of 6.6811, signalling the central bank's preference for a more gradual pace of currency appreciation.

**Read more:**US stocks today: Nasdaq rebounds as chipmakers rally, Apple slides ahead of US midterm results

Meanwhile, the CFETS yuan basket index, which measures the currency against a basket of trading partners' currencies, declined to 103.75 based on Wednesday's official guidance, according to Reuters calculations using official data. The index had touched a 52-month high on Tuesday but remains up around 5.9% so far this year.

**Read more:**Global Market Today: Asian shares retreat as US futures slide on mid-term election bets

Separately, investors are closely tracking the outcome of the US midterm elections and their potential implications for global currency markets. Market participants have been positioning for a strong Democratic showing, as the results could influence expectations around US fiscal policy, political uncertainty and the dollar's direction.

title: Enhancing domestic value in exports.
content_md:
|  |
| The scale of imports and exports exceeded 1 trillion USD, but the FDI sector held nearly 785 billion USD. |

This was the statement made by Mr. Nguyen Anh Son, Director of the Import-Export Department ( Ministry of Industry and Trade ), when assessing the milestone of Vietnam's foreign trade reaching and exceeding 1,000 billion USD.

**Foreign direct investment (FDI) enterprises contributed nearly $785 billion.**

According to the General Statistics Office, in the first 10 months of 2026, Vietnam's total import and export turnover of goods exceeded 1 trillion USD, an increase of 32.3% compared to the same period last year. This is a particularly significant milestone for the economy , demonstrating the scale and increasingly deep integration of the Vietnamese economy into international trade.

Trade surpassed $1 trillion with only two months left in the year, clearly demonstrating the recovery and sustained growth of domestic production, especially in the processing and manufacturing industries – the key export sectors.

Over the past 10 months, many key export product groups have recorded high growth rates.

Leading the way were electronics, computers, and components with a turnover of $149.4 billion, a 71% increase compared to the same period last year. Machinery, equipment, tools, and spare parts reached $63.268 billion, a 30.4% increase; telephones and components reached $57.6 billion, an 18.4% increase; and transportation vehicles and parts reached nearly $17 billion, a 17.1% increase. Wood and wood products also brought in over $15 billion, a 6.8% increase.

This result demonstrates the continued expansion of production capacity and reflects the ability of businesses to capitalize on opportunities arising from international market demand. As a result, export turnover maintained positive growth momentum, making a significant contribution to the country's record trade volume.

However, behind the impressive growth picture, the contribution of the domestic business sector remains "thin".

Statistics show that the foreign direct investment (FDI) sector achieved a total import and export turnover of US$784.86 billion (including crude oil), accounting for 77.6% of the country's total import and export turnover. Meanwhile, the domestic enterprise sector only achieved US$225.69 billion, equivalent to 22.4%.

Notably, the gap is even more pronounced in export activities. Exports from the domestic business sector reached $93.93 billion, an increase of 8.2%, accounting for only 18.8% of total export turnover. Conversely, the FDI sector reached $405.31 billion, an increase of 33%, accounting for as much as 81.2%.

The FDI sector also holds an overwhelming share in the export turnover of many key industries, especially electronics, machinery, equipment, and spare parts. These three product groups alone brought in over $270 billion, accounting for approximately 54% of the country's total export turnover.

**Increase the Vietnamese value content in export goods.**

Commenting on the milestone of foreign trade exceeding 1 trillion USD, Mr. Nguyen Anh Son stated that the greater challenge is not only maintaining the scale of growth but also improving the quality of growth, increasing the value created domestically, reducing dependence on external supply sources, and enhancing the position of Vietnamese businesses in the global value chain.

According to Mr. Son, the value added generated domestically is not commensurate with the scale of export turnover, especially in some high-value sectors such as electronics, machinery, equipment, textiles, and footwear. The capacity of domestic enterprises to participate in global supply chains remains limited.

The main reason stems from production capacity and the ability to meet the requirements of international markets and corporations. Many Vietnamese businesses, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, have not fully met the requirements regarding production scale, technical standards, quality management, technological innovation, and supply chain stability.

Furthermore, the linkages between domestic businesses and FDI have not met expectations. Although FDI contributes a large portion of export turnover, the ability to connect, transfer technology, and develop a domestic supplier ecosystem is still not commensurate with the scale of operations of these businesses.

Some export-oriented manufacturing sectors still rely heavily on imported raw materials and components, resulting in limited domestic value creation and a low spillover effect on the economy.

This reality necessitates a shift in the export growth model. Instead of primarily relying on expanding production, processing, and assembly capacity, Vietnam needs to increase the localization rate, develop its capacity to supply raw materials and components, and gradually participate in higher value-added stages.

To gradually address these shortcomings, the Ministry of Industry and Trade stated that it will continue to promote the development of supporting industries, focusing on sectors with high potential for value-added creation such as electronics, semiconductors, precision mechanics, electrical equipment, and processing industries.

This is coupled with solutions to enhance the capacity of Vietnamese businesses through support for technological innovation, improved governance, meeting international standards, and increasing their ability to participate more deeply in global supply chains.

Another important task is to promote linkages between FDI enterprises and domestic enterprises. Strengthening connections between the two sectors will create conditions for Vietnamese enterprises to gradually become suppliers of raw materials, components, services, and input products for multinational corporations, instead of only participating in low value-added stages.

Regarding attracting FDI, according to Mr. Nguyen Anh Son, it is necessary to continue orienting projects with high technological content, committed to developing the domestic supply chain ecosystem, and capable of creating a spillover effect on the economy. Because the long-term goal is not simply to continue increasing export turnover, but more importantly, to enhance the Vietnamese value content in each product.

title: Bank capital flows contributed to stabilizing the market at the end of the year in Ho Chi Minh City.
content_md:
The market stabilization program aims to ensure that the city's residents have access to essential goods and consumer products at reasonable, stable, and lower prices than the general market average. This is especially significant during the end of the year, holidays, and the Lunar New Year – not only reflecting the city's humanitarian spirit, but also contributing significantly to price stability and the effectiveness of monetary policy. Furthermore, if the program is large-scale and implemented effectively in distribution, supply chain linkages, and connecting supply and demand, it will be even more impactful.

Not only does it reflect the humane spirit of a compassionate city in ensuring social welfare during the year-end period, the market stabilization program in Ho Chi Minh City also demonstrates the practical effectiveness of the close connection between bank capital, distribution activities, and modern payment solutions.

From the perspective of supporting businesses in reducing costs and improving capital efficiency, this contributes to lowering input costs and product prices, ensuring reasonable and stable selling prices. This result is largely due to the crucial role of the banking sector in Ho Chi Minh City, particularly credit institutions that provide loans for market stabilization programs and offer cashless payment services to businesses and distribution, retail, and wholesale systems in the area. This is demonstrated through three pillars:

Firstly, the program aims to best meet the capital needs of businesses in the stabilization sector. Credit funds are concentrated on businesses participating in the program, particularly those involved in production, processing, consumption, and distribution. To date, cumulative loan disbursements under the program, from the beginning of 2026, have reached VND 16,800 billion, benefiting 31 businesses, with a total outstanding loan balance of VND 7,766 billion.

Of this, short-term loans, with a total outstanding balance of VND 7,675 billion, accounted for 98.8% of the total outstanding loans under the price stabilization program. This result is consistent with the program's requirements and the characteristics of production, business, and product distribution of enterprises in the value chain and the supply-demand connection activities of the city.

| Illustrative image |

Secondly, the low interest rates on loans to businesses participating in the program enable them to reduce borrowing costs, thereby lowering product prices and maintaining price stability for goods included in the program. Currently, interest rates range from 6.5%-8% per year for short-term loans and 8.8%-9.8% per year for long-term loans, directly supporting businesses with borrowing costs, facilitating cost reductions, efficient capital utilization, and thus encouraging active participation in the program.

Thirdly, credit institutions best meet the service needs of customers and businesses participating in the program. In particular, product distribution businesses, supermarkets and retail stores, as well as citizens and workers in industrial zones and export processing zones; and people in difficult circumstances… (who are the beneficiaries of the year-end support policy) all implement and use cashless payment methods.

The use of modern banking products and services not only facilitates sales growth and the implementation of market stabilization programs, but also enables businesses, especially trading and distribution companies and supermarkets, to improve capital efficiency and business performance during peak seasons such as the Lunar New Year.

These positive results will continue to be promoted and enhanced by specific solutions from the City's banking sector in the remaining months of the year: connecting banks and businesses; participating in consumer stimulus programs and supply-demand connection activities of the Department of Industry and Trade… and promoting cashless payments at points of sale, tourist destinations, shopping centers, etc., in order to contribute to maintaining stable commodity prices and maximizing the effectiveness of monetary policy in the final months of the year.

title: Ho Chi Minh City announces three-tier investment incentives to boost FDI attraction
content_md:
The Ho Chi Minh City Investment Cooperation Forum 2026, themed "Ho Chi Minh City - New Development Space - New Investment Cooperation Opportunities," was organized on November 2 by the Ho Chi Minh City Investment and Trade Promotion Center (ITPC) with support from Fortune Asia magazine.

#### Three-tier incentives to attract high-quality capital

Speaking at the forum, Mr. Nguyen Loc Ha, Permanent Vice Chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee, stated that in the first ten months of 2026, Ho Chi Minh City attracted $19.1 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI), exceeding the annual plan by 73.9 percent. The city currently has over 22,036 active FDI projects with total registered capital of more than $157.4 billion.

Additionally, the city's appeal stems from its position as an economic center, a large consumer market, and a dynamic business community. Notably, after merging with Binh Duong and Ba Ria - Vung Tau, Ho Chi Minh City has expanded its development space, encompassing finance, services, innovation, modern industry, and deep-water ports.

Specifically, the city's attractiveness comes from three tiers of investment incentives aimed at enhancing FDI attraction.

The first tier includes national incentives for priority sectors such as high technology, research and development (R&D), and the semiconductor industry. New projects in these fields enjoy a corporate income tax rate of 10 percent for 15 years, a four-year tax exemption, and a 50 percent tax reduction for the following nine years.

The second tier involves Ho Chi Minh City's specific mechanisms, as stipulated in the Urban Development Law effective from October 1, 2026. Strategic investors are prioritized in customs procedures, human resource development support, R&D, and other incentives within the city's decision-making authority.

The third tier offers incentives in special institutional spaces. Members of the Vietnam International Financial Center in Ho Chi Minh City operating in priority sectors are subject to a 10 percent corporate income tax rate for 30 years. Experts and managers working at the Center are exempt from personal income tax until the end of 2030.

Mr. Andrew Staples, Editorial Director of Fortune Asia, shared insights on the contribution of Vietnamese businesses in the region, noting that the Fortune Southeast Asia 500 ranking in 2026 includes 72 Vietnamese enterprises with a combined revenue of $177.9 billion, a 10.5 percent increase, tribling the average growth rate in Southeast Asia.

Vietnamese businesses contribute about 25 percent of the revenue growth. This is also one of the reasons Fortune chose Ho Chi Minh City to host the Fortune Southeast Asia 500 Summit for the first time, Mr. Andrew Staples noted.

**Capital shifts towards high-tech, infrastructure, and logistics**

According to Mr. Pham Quang Nhat, Director of the Ho Chi Minh City Investment and Trade Promotion Center (ITPC), the capital structure in 2026 shows three notable trends.

First, capital is concentrated in high technology and digital infrastructure. In the first nine months of 2026, the Ho Chi Minh City High-Tech Park attracted $1.23 billion in new capital, averaging over $300 million per project.

Second, capital is directed towards infrastructure and logistics. The Can Gio International Transshipment Port project, with total investment of over $4.9 billion, has just been granted an investment registration certificate, involving a leading global container port operator.

Third, additional capital and activities of capital contribution and share purchase continue to be recorded. In the first ten months of 2026, ongoing projects in the city registered nearly $5.7 billion in additional capital; more than 1,611 foreign investors contributed capital and purchased shares in domestic enterprises.

During the direct dialogue session with the investor community, representatives from international associations and businesses shared investment experiences, assessed the business environment, and explored cooperation potential in the city.

Additionally, the forum helped connect investor needs with Ho Chi Minh City's development orientation, incentive mechanisms, and new cooperation spaces.

Representatives from international business associations also shared key market insights. Mr. Travis Mitchell of AmCham Vietnam evaluated the local business climate, while Mr. Wesley Chua from SingCham focused on services, logistics, and infrastructure opportunities.

Additionally, Mr. Kulachet Dharachandra, Country Director of SCG Vietnam, discussed strategic industrial investments and green transformation.

#### Fortune 500 Southeast Asia Summit held in Ho Chi Minh City for the first time

The Fortune 500 Southeast Asia Summit is a testament to Ho Chi Minh City's appeal to international investors. The city is committed to transparency and responsibility, aiming to attract long-term investment partners and contribute to sustainable development value creation.

This forum focused on discussing investment attraction directions, cooperation opportunities in Ho Chi Minh City's new development space, and solutions to enhance connections between domestic businesses and international investors.
topic: TP.HCM công bố ưu đãi đầu tư ba cấp để thu hút FDI
summary: Diễn đàn Hợp tác Đầu tư TP. Hồ Chí Minh 2026 do ITPC tổ chức ngày 2/11 với sự hỗ trợ của tạp chí Fortune Asia.

Theo ông Nguyễn Lộc Hà, trong 10 tháng đầu năm 2026 TP. Hồ Chí Minh thu hút 19,1 tỷ USD vốn FDI, vượt kế hoạch năm 73,9%; thành phố có hơn 22.036 dự án FDI còn hiệu lực với tổng vốn đăng ký hơn 157,4 tỷ USD.

Thành phố nêu ba tầng ưu đãi: ưu đãi quốc gia cho lĩnh vực ưu tiên (thuế thu nhập doanh nghiệp 10% trong 15 năm, miễn thuế 4 năm, giảm 50% trong 9 năm tiếp theo), cơ chế riêng theo Luật Phát triển đô thị có hiệu lực từ 1/10/2026, và ưu đãi tại Trung tâm tài chính quốc tế Việt Nam (thuế thu nhập doanh nghiệp 10% trong 30 năm, chuyên gia miễn thuế thu nhập cá nhân đến hết 2030).
Theo Fortune Asia, bảng xếp hạng Fortune Southeast Asia 500 năm 2026 có 72 doanh nghiệp Việt Nam với tổng doanh thu 177,9 tỷ USD, tăng 10,5%.

Theo ông Phạm Quang Nhật, 9 tháng đầu năm Khu Công nghệ cao TP. Hồ Chí Minh thu hút 1,23 tỷ USD vốn mới; dự án Cảng trung chuyển quốc tế Cần Giờ vốn hơn 4,9 tỷ USD vừa được cấp giấy chứng nhận đăng ký đầu tư.
Trong 10 tháng đầu năm, các dự án đang hoạt động đăng ký tăng thêm gần 5,7 tỷ USD và hơn 1.611 nhà đầu tư nước ngoài góp vốn, mua cổ phần doanh nghiệp trong nước.

#### ConocoPhillips beats estimates on higher oil prices, raises dividend

By

PublishedNov 05, 2026, 07:42 AM

ConocoPhillips beats estimates on higher oil prices, raises dividend

© Reuters.

In this article:

Nov 5 (Reuters) - ConocoPhillips raised its quarterly dividend after beating Wall Street estimates for third-quarter adjusted profit on Thursday, as stronger commodity prices and cost-cutting measures helped offset a decline in its output.

Shares of the largest US independent oil and gas producer were up 2.3% in morning trading.

What metrics indicate ConocoPhillips can sustain its dividend increase?How did higher oil prices drive COP's earnings beat?

Benchmark Brent crude averaged about $89.27 per barrel during the July-to-September period, up more than 31% from a year earlier, driven by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East that raised concerns about global oil supplies.

The company’s average realized price was $61.40 per barrel of oil equivalent for the quarter, 32% higher than a year earlier.

Quarterly production was 2.3 million barrels of oil equivalent per day (boepd), compared with 2.4 million boepd a year earlier.

ConocoPhillips forecast fourth-quarter production between 2.32 million boepd and 2.36 million boepd. It raised its quarterly dividend by nearly 11% to 93 cents per share from 84 cents previously.

Last year, ConocoPhillips said it would cut 20% to 25% of its workforce to streamline operations and reduce costs following its acquisition of Marathon Oil. In October, it informed employees and contractors in Canada of workforce reductions.

The company also said it was evaluating a potential sale of its Norway business and the Teesside asset in the UK after receiving an unsolicited offer, although it did not identify the bidder or disclose financial details.

ConocoPhillips’ quarterly net income more than doubled to $4 billion year-on-year, boosted by higher oil prices amid supply concerns driven by the Middle East conflict.

title: FOMC May Need to Tighten Monetary Policy Gradually to Combat Inflation, Cleveland Fed's Hammack Says
content_md:
The Federal Reserve may need to continue raising interest rates to curb inflation, though at a gradual pace to minimize economic disruptions, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said Thursday.

Last month, the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee held its benchmark lending rate steady, following a 25-basis-point hike in September. Hammack and Fed Governor Lisa Cook preferred a second consecutive quarter-percentage-point hike at the October meeting.

Inflationary pressures have intensified this year and appear relatively broad-based, Hammack said Thursday in remarks prepared for delivery at an event in Switzerland, citing September data. "Inflation has now been above our (2%) goal for nearly six years," she said.

The headline personal consumption expenditure price index rose 3.6% year over year in September, following a 3.4% gain the prior month. The core measure -- which excludes the volatile food and energy components -- increased to 3.1% from 3%, official data showed last month.

"I expect that monetary policy will need to move to a restrictive stance to bring inflation back to 2% in a timely manner," Hammack said Thursday. "I prefer getting to that stance through more frequent smaller adjustments when possible, something which would be less disruptive to households, businesses, and financial markets."

Gradual rate hikes should minimize the risk of the policy falling behind where it needs to be and an inflationary mindset becoming entrenched, Hammack said, without specifying when the Fed might resume policy tightening.

The FOMC's Summary of Economic Projections released in September indicated that policymakers were anticipating another rate hike by the end of this year.

Markets are pricing in a 69% probability that the Fed will raise interest rate by 25 basis points in December, with the remaining odds in favor of a pause, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Last week, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the FOMC will likely need to tighten monetary policy "soon" to bring inflation down to its 2% goal in a timely manner.
